## §16. The Question of Brownian Motion Within Navier–Stokes: The Orthodox-Literature Onsager–Machlup / Landau–Lifshitz / Betchov / Bandak–Goldenfeld–Mailybaev–Eyink Phenomenological Tradition and the Structural-Foundational Gap the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic Closes

### §16.1. The Question Posed: Has the Orthodox Navier–Stokes Literature Ever Considered Brownian Motion of the Air Molecules?

A fluid is composed of molecules. Every molecule of the fluid is, under the foundational reading of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic supplied by [29, Theorem 6] and [27, §3.2 and §4], subject to Brownian motion driven by Compton coupling to the McGucken Sphere expansion at every spacetime event. The Brownian motion is not a phenomenological feature added on to the molecules' dynamics — it is a foundational structural feature of the dynamics derived from dx₄/dt = ic via the spatial projection of the spherically symmetric x₄-expansion at every event of every molecule.

The structural question of the present section is: **has the orthodox Navier–Stokes literature ever recognized that every molecule of the fluid is subject to Brownian motion, and has the orthodox literature ever traced this Brownian motion to a foundational principle?**

The orthodox-literature answer foundationally is: **the orthodox literature has recognized the phenomenon of Brownian motion of the constituent molecules of a fluid, but has not traced it to a foundational geometric principle.** The orthodox treatment is phenomenological: the thermal noise is introduced as a stochastic correction to the deterministic Navier–Stokes equation with covariance prescribed by the fluctuation-dissipation theorem and the Gibbs invariant measure, with the structural origin of the noise left as a postulated consequence of unspecified molecular dynamics.

### §16.2. The Orthodox Literature: Onsager–Machlup 1953, Landau–Lifshitz 1957, Betchov 1957–1965, Bandak–Goldenfeld–Mailybaev–Eyink 2022

The orthodox phenomenological tradition recognising Brownian-motion / stochastic-noise content within deterministic physical evolution equations traces through four primary sources, each cited verbatim below, with the Onsager–Machlup 1953 paper [55] identified as the *founding move* of the tradition — predating the Landau–Lifshitz 1957 fluctuating-hydrodynamics framework by four years and supplying the structural template (explicit Gaussian stochastic noise added to deterministic evolution equations with covariance prescribed by fluctuation-dissipation considerations) that the entire subsequent tradition operates within.

**(OL0) Onsager–Machlup 1953 — *Physical Review* 91, 1505: The Founding Move of the Phenomenological Stochastic-Noise-Within-Physical-Evolution-Equations Tradition.** Lars Onsager and Stefan Machlup published in *Physical Review* in 1953 [55] the paper *"Fluctuations and Irreversible Processes"*, extending Onsager's original 1931 reciprocal-relations theory of linear irreversible thermodynamics [53, 55] to incorporate fluctuation-level dynamics. The structural content of the 1953 paper is articulated verbatim in [52, §A, footnote 8, p.10]:

> *"in 1953 Onsager (together with S. Machlup) extended his original theory in response to a related challenge. While the reciprocal relations predict the average behavior of a system – for example, the mean heat flux or mean diffusion current – the underlying dynamics of the fluctuations that give rise to the averages were not taken into account. The extended theory introduced an explicit random Gaussian noise into the formalism, allowing for the calculation of the probability paths of a given state variable."*

The Onsager–Machlup 1953 framework introduces explicit Gaussian-fluctuation content into the linear-irreversible-thermodynamics evolution equations and establishes the structural template — *"explicit random Gaussian noise into the formalism"* — that the subsequent fluctuating-hydrodynamics tradition of Landau–Lifshitz 1957, Betchov 1957–1965, and Bandak–Goldenfeld–Mailybaev–Eyink 2022 operates within. The Onsager–Machlup framework is the *founding move* of the phenomenological-stochastic-noise-within-Navier–Stokes tradition: every subsequent contribution adds explicit Gaussian noise to the deterministic evolution equation with covariance prescribed by fluctuation-dissipation considerations, following the structural template laid down by Onsager and Machlup in 1953.

**The limit of the Onsager–Machlup framework.** The Gaussian-fluctuation content of Onsager–Machlup 1953 is *phenomenologically introduced*: the noise is added to the equations as a stochastic correction with covariance fixed by the fluctuation-dissipation relation. The structural origin of the noise — the foundational geometric principle that generates the fluctuations in the first place — is *not addressed* by the Onsager–Machlup framework. The fluctuations are postulated as a phenomenological consequence of unspecified microscopic dynamics; they are not derived theorems of any foundational principle. The same limit propagates through every subsequent contribution to the tradition, including the Landau–Lifshitz 1957 hydrodynamic specialisation per (OL1) below, the Betchov 1957–1965 incompressible-fluid specialisation per (OL2) below, and the Bandak–Goldenfeld–Mailybaev–Eyink 2022 dissipation-range quantitative result per (OL3) below.

**(OL1) Landau–Lifshitz 1957, *Fluid Mechanics*, Chapter XVII.** Landau and Lifshitz [12] introduced the fluctuating-hydrodynamics framework in 1957 in their monograph *Fluid Mechanics*, Chapter XVII, extending the deterministic Navier–Stokes equation by adding a Gaussian-fluctuating stress term ∇ · τ with covariance prescribed by the fluctuation-dissipation theorem [11, Eq. (1.2)–(1.3)]:

$$\partial_t u + (u \cdot \nabla) u = -\nabla p + \nu \Delta u + \nabla \cdot \tau,$$

$$\langle \tau_{ij}(x,t) \tau_{kl}(x',t')\rangle = \frac{2 \nu k_B T}{\rho}\left(\delta_{ik}\delta_{jl} + \delta_{il}\delta_{jk} - \tfrac{2}{3} \delta_{ij}\delta_{kl}\right) \delta^3(x - x') \delta(t - t').$$

The Landau–Lifshitz framework has the Gibbs distribution P_G[u] = (1/Z) exp(-ρ ∫ |u(x)|² d³ x/(2 k_B T)) as an invariant measure. The Landau–Lifshitz framework recognises that the orthodox deterministic Navier–Stokes equation is *incomplete* at the molecular scale: thermal noise driven by molecular Brownian motion must be added to the equation for the equation to describe real fluids correctly at small scales.

**The limit of the Landau–Lifshitz framework.** The stochastic term ∇ · τ is *phenomenologically derived*: it is constructed by requiring the resulting stochastic-PDE to have the Gibbs distribution as invariant measure, with the covariance fixed by the fluctuation-dissipation theorem. The structural origin of the noise — the foundational geometric principle that generates the molecular Brownian motion in the first place — is *not addressed* by the Landau–Lifshitz framework. The thermal noise is a postulated phenomenological consequence of unspecified molecular dynamics; it is not a derived theorem of any foundational principle.

**(OL2) Betchov 1957–1965 — independent derivation of fluctuating hydrodynamics for incompressible fluids.** Robert Betchov, in a series of papers from 1957 through 1965 [13, 14, 15], independently developed the fluctuating-hydrodynamics framework specifically for incompressible fluids. Betchov's contribution, articulated by Bandak et al. 2022 verbatim from [11, Section I, paragraph 8]:

> *"Betchov not only recognized the significant effects that thermal noise could have on dissipation-range statistics and other phenomena in fluid turbulence, such as transition and predictability, but he also developed the dx₄/dt = ic framework of fluctuating hydrodynamics for incompressible fluids, independent of Landau and Lifschitz."*

Betchov's closing observation, transcribed verbatim from [13] via the citation in [11, p. 2]: *"the gap between turbulence and molecular agitation may not be as wide as is generally appreciated."*

**The limit of the Betchov framework.** Betchov's framework, like the Landau–Lifshitz framework, treats the thermal noise as a phenomenological consequence of unspecified molecular dynamics. Betchov did not address the structural origin of the molecular Brownian motion; he assumed it as input from kinetic theory and computed its consequences for the turbulent dissipation range.

**(OL3) Bandak–Goldenfeld–Mailybaev–Eyink 2022 — *Physical Review E* 105, 065113.** Bandak, Goldenfeld, Mailybaev, and Eyink published in *Physical Review E* on 29 June 2022 the paper *"Dissipation-range fluid turbulence and thermal noise"* [11], which is the most recent definitive statement of the orthodox-literature position on the role of thermal noise (i.e., molecular Brownian motion) in the Navier–Stokes equation. The structural content of the 2022 paper is articulated verbatim from the abstract:

> *"We revisit the issue of whether thermal fluctuations are relevant for incompressible fluid turbulence and estimate the scale at which they become important. As anticipated by Betchov in a prescient series of works more than six decades ago, this scale is about equal to the Kolmogorov length, even though that is several orders of magnitude above the mean free path. This result implies that the deterministic version of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equation is inadequate to describe the dissipation range of turbulence in molecular fluids."*

The structural fact established by [11] is the *scale* at which thermal noise (i.e., molecular Brownian motion) becomes dominant in the Navier–Stokes equation: **the Kolmogorov length η = ν^{3/4} ε^{-1/4}, which is several orders of magnitude above the molecular mean free path.** Specifically, [11, Section II.B] computes for the turbulent atmospheric boundary layer (ABL) at ε = 400\ cm²/s³, ν = 0.15\ cm²/s, ρ = 1.2 × 10⁻³\ g/cm³, T = 300\ K the Kolmogorov length η = 0.54 mm and the equipartition length ℓ_{eq} ∼ η/11 ≈ 49\ μm, compared to the mean-free-path of air at room temperature and standard atmospheric pressure λ_{mfp} = 68 nm. **The thermal-noise-dominated length scale is approximately three orders of magnitude above the mean free path** (49\ μm / 68\ nm ≈ 720).

The structural consequence articulated by [11, Section I, paragraph 3], transcribed verbatim:

> *"There are effects intrinsic to molecular fluids that are omitted, however, by the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, most importantly thermal fluctuations [13,14]. These effects are described instead by an extension of the usual deterministic fluid equations known as fluctuating hydrodynamics, originally due to Landau and Lifschitz [15], Ch. XVII."*

**The limit of the Bandak–Goldenfeld–Mailybaev–Eyink framework.** The 2022 paper establishes that the deterministic Navier–Stokes equation of [1] is structurally inadequate to describe real fluids at scales near and below the Kolmogorov length, with thermal noise — i.e., molecular Brownian motion — becoming the dominant effect at ℓ_{eq} ∼ η/11, three orders of magnitude above the molecular mean free path. **The thermal noise itself is, in the 2022 paper as in the Landau–Lifshitz and Betchov predecessors, a phenomenological consequence of unspecified molecular dynamics.** The 2022 paper traces the *consequences* of thermal noise in detail (Kolmogorov-scale equipartition, k² thermal spectrum, breaking of K41 scaling, modifications of intermittency) but does not trace the thermal noise to a foundational geometric principle.

### §16.4. Theorem 17 — The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic as the Foundational Closure of the Onsager–Machlup / Landau–Lifshitz / Betchov / Bandak–Goldenfeld–Mailybaev–Eyink Phenomenological Tradition

### §17.1. The 2025 Clay Research Conference and Šverák's Plenary Report at the 25-Year Millennium Anniversary

The 2025 Clay Research Conference, held at the Andrew Wiles Building, Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford, on Wednesday 1 and Thursday 2 October 2025, was constituted as the official Clay Mathematics Institute commemoration of the 25-year anniversary of the Millennium Prize Problems. Per the Clay Mathematics Institute conference programme [63, verbatim]: *"The 2025 Clay Research Conference will be held on Wednesday, 1 and Thursday, 2 October in L1 of the Andrew Wiles Building. Plenary talks will celebrate the Millennium Prize Problems and reflect on progress in the past 25 years."* The official Clay-sanctioned plenary speaker on the Navier–Stokes problem at the 25-year anniversary was Vladimír Šverák (Distinguished McKnight University Professor of Mathematics at the University of Minnesota), with the talk titled *"A report on the Navier-Stokes Problem"* delivered as the opening plenary session of the conference on the morning of Wednesday 1 October 2025, per [62]. ### §17A.1. The Four Open Problems and the Structural Identification

Four foundational problems have remained open across the orthodox theoretical-physics literature, each in a distinct tradition, each treated by the orthodox community as a separate problem belonging to its own subfield, and each consequently never identified as an instance of the same underlying structural non-recognition. The four problems, in the order of their historical emergence, are:

**(I) The Carnot–Clausius–Boltzmann second-law reversibility paradox (1824–1872–1876–present).** Carnot 1824 articulated the empirical irreversibility of heat-engine cycles in *Réflexions sur la puissance motrice du feu* [84]: heat flows spontaneously from hot to cold and not the other way around, and a maximum efficiency exists for any thermodynamic cycle that cannot be exceeded by any engineering arrangement. Clausius 1850 formalized this as the Second Law of Thermodynamics and in 1865 coined the term *entropy* (German *Entropie*) for the macroscopic quantity whose monotone increase characterizes the irreversibility [85, 84]. Boltzmann 1872 in *Weitere Studien über das Wärmegleichgewicht unter Gasmolekülen* [87] derived from kinetic theory the H-theorem — the *Stosszahlansatz*-based result that the H-functional H(t) = ∫ f(v, t) log f(v, t) dv satisfies dH/dt ≤ 0 under the Boltzmann transport equation, equivalent to dS/dt ≥ 0 with S = -k_B H. Loschmidt 1876 in *Über den Zustand des Wärmegleichgewichtes eines Systems von Körpern mit Rücksicht auf die Schwerkraft* [88] raised the reversibility objection: no theorem deduced from time-reversible Newtonian mechanics can produce a time-asymmetric conclusion, because for every trajectory along which the H-functional decreases monotonically there is, by reversal of all velocities, an equally-valid Newtonian trajectory along which H increases monotonically. Boltzmann 1877 responded in *Bemerkungen über einige Probleme der mechanischen Wärmetheorie* [89] and *Über die Beziehung zwischen dem zweiten Hauptsatze der mechanischen Wärmetheorie und der Wahrscheinlichkeitsrechnung respektive den Sätzen über das Wärmegleichgewicht* [90] with a statistical reinterpretation: entropy is identified with the logarithm of the multiplicity, S = k_B log W (the formula carved on Boltzmann's tombstone in Vienna), and the H-theorem is to be read as a statement about *the overwhelming statistical likelihood* of the macrostate at the end of the trajectory rather than as a strict theorem of Newtonian dynamics. Burbury 1894 [91] and Bryan 1894 [92] identified the implicit time-asymmetry in the *Stosszahlansatz* (the molecular-chaos assumption that pre-collision molecular velocities are uncorrelated; the same assumption applied to post-collision velocities would have produced dH/dt ≥ 0 by the same argument). The foundational question — what is the geometric source of the strict-positive dS/dt at every event, given that the underlying microscopic dynamics is strict-time-reversible — has remained open in the orthodox literature for one hundred and fifty years. It is conventionally referred to as "the problem of the arrow of time" or "the reversibility paradox" and is the subject of an extensive contemporary literature [93, 92, 93, 94, 95, 96, 97]; no orthodox resolution generally regarded as foundationally complete has emerged.

**(II) The Schrödinger–Born–von Neumann quantum measurement problem (1926–present).** Schrödinger 1926 in *Quantisierung als Eigenwertproblem* [100] derived the linear, deterministic, time-reversible wave equation $i\hbar \, \partial_t \psi = H\psi$ that governs the unitary continuous evolution of quantum states. Born 1926 in *Zur Quantenmechanik der Stoßvorgänge* [101] introduced the statistical interpretation of the wave function: the integral $\int_V |\psi(x)|^2 \, dx$ is the probability that a particle in the state $\psi$ is observed in the region $V$. Heisenberg 1927 in *Über den anschaulichen Inhalt der quantentheoretischen Kinematik und Mechanik* [102] articulated the uncertainty relations. von Neumann 1932 in *Mathematische Grundlagen der Quantenmechanik* [103] formalized the orthodox structure with explicit distinction between two types of state evolution: **Type I evolution**, the continuous unitary $\psi(t) \to U(t) \psi(0)$ with $U(t) U(t)^\dagger = I$, generated by the Hamiltonian via Schrödinger; and **Type II evolution**, the discontinuous projection $\psi \to P_a \psi / \|P_a \psi\|$ that takes place when the system is measured and the outcome $a$ is observed. The apparent contradiction — Type I is strict-time-reversible-unitary while Type II is strict-time-asymmetric-non-unitary — is the core content of the *quantum measurement problem*. The orthodox literature has produced multiple competing interpretations, none of which has produced a foundationally complete resolution generally accepted by the physics community:

- the *Copenhagen interpretation* [104, 103] (Bohr 1928, Heisenberg 1927), in which Type II evolution is taken as a primitive that does not require derivation from Type I and that requires an external "classical apparatus" to define;
- the *pilot-wave interpretation* [106, 105] (de Broglie 1927, Bohm 1952), in which determinism is restored by postulating hidden trajectories guided by the wave function, at the cost of explicit non-locality;
- the *many-worlds interpretation* [108] (Everett 1957), in which Type II evolution is denied entirely and the universal wave function is taken to evolve only by Type I, with the appearance of Type II projection reinterpreted as relative-state branching;
- *decoherence-based interpretations* [109, 108, 109, 110] (Zeh 1970, Zurek 1981/1991/2003), in which Type II evolution is reinterpreted as an effective phenomenon arising from Type I evolution of the system + environment, with the off-diagonal density-matrix elements decaying rapidly due to entanglement with environmental degrees of freedom.

The orthodox literature contains repeated explicit acknowledgments that the measurement problem remains unresolved. Bell 1990 in *Against "Measurement"* [113] wrote of "the unprofessionally vague and ambiguous" character of orthodox measurement-language. Leggett 2005 in *The Quantum Measurement Problem* [114] referred to it as "the most stubbornly persistent intellectual scandal in physics." Weinberg 2017 in *The Trouble with Quantum Mechanics* [115] wrote that "I'm not as convinced as I used to be of the supreme reliability of conventional quantum mechanics" and described the measurement problem as "still completely unresolved." The question — what is the foundational-geometric source of the asymmetry between Type I and Type II evolution — has remained open for ninety-eight years.

**(III) The Lorenz deterministic-chaos problem (1963–present).** Lorenz 1963 in *Deterministic Nonperiodic Flow* [116] published in *Journal of the Atmospheric Sciences* (volume 20, pages 130–141) demonstrated that finite systems of purely deterministic, non-linear ordinary differential equations can exhibit *sensitive dependence on initial conditions* — exponential divergence of trajectories starting from initial conditions differing by an arbitrarily small amount, leading to macroscopic unpredictability over finite forecast horizons despite the equations themselves containing no random or stochastic element. The opening sentence of the abstract of [116] is verbatim: *"Finite systems of deterministic ordinary nonlinear differential equations may be designed to represent forced dissipative hydrodynamic flow."* The 1963 paper was cited only three times outside meteorology during 1963–1973 [117] but emerged in the 1970s and 1980s as the foundation of classical chaos theory [118, 117, 118, 119]. Lorenz himself in 1972 popularized the phenomenon under the name *butterfly effect* [122], the title of his lecture to the American Association for the Advancement of Science being *"Predictability: Does the Flap of a Butterfly's Wings in Brazil Set off a Tornado in Texas?"* The foundational question — *what is the physical source of the sensitive dependence, given that the dynamical equations themselves are time-symmetric Hamiltonian flows with no stochastic content* — has remained open in the orthodox literature for sixty-one years. The conventional orthodox treatment refers to "deterministic randomness" or "the butterfly effect" or "sensitive dependence on initial conditions" without identification of a foundational-geometric origin for why the sensitive dependence is exhibited *physically* by real fluid systems rather than only by their mathematical idealizations. The identification of the source of sensitive dependence as the McGucken-Compton stream operating at every spacetime event from dx₄/dt = ic, supplying continuous perturbations that physically realize the mathematically-possible exponential divergence at every event, is the McGucken-framework closure of the open question.

**(IV) The Cauchy–Stokes–Leray–Fefferman Navier–Stokes smoothness-vs-blowup problem (1828–2000–present).** Cauchy 1828 in *Sur les équations qui expriment les conditions d'équilibre, ou les lois du mouvement intérieur d'un corps solide, élastique ou non élastique* [123] established the stress-tensor framework for continuum mechanics. Navier 1822 [124] and independently Stokes 1845 [125] added the viscous Laplacian term $\nu \Delta u$ to the time-symmetric inviscid Euler equation of 1755 [126], producing what is now called the Navier–Stokes equation. The structural feature that *the viscous term was added phenomenologically to a time-symmetric foundational equation, without identification of its foundational-geometric source*, is the same structural feature that Boltzmann 1872 [87] faced in attempting to derive the second law from time-symmetric Newtonian mechanics. Leray 1934 in *Sur le mouvement d'un liquide visqueux emplissant l'espace* [127] established the global existence of weak (Leray–Hopf) solutions but did not establish their smoothness. Hopf 1951 [128] proved the energy inequality. Ladyzhenskaya 1969 in *The Mathematical Theory of Viscous Incompressible Flow* [129] produced the canonical orthodox treatment of the PDE problem. Beale–Kato–Majda 1984 [130] established the blowup criterion. Fefferman 2000 [1] articulated the Clay Millennium Prize Problem statement. Tao 2016 [19] demonstrated that an averaged variant of the equation admits finite-time blowup via a self-replicating fluid von Neumann machine architecture. Wang–Buckmaster–Gómez-Serrano–Lai 2025 [25] discovered unstable singularities. The foundational question — *what is the foundational-geometric source of the viscous Laplacian $\nu \Delta u$ that the orthodox tradition has treated phenomenologically since 1822* — has remained open in the orthodox literature for two hundred and two years, and the related PDE-level question of global smoothness has remained open since the Clay 2000 articulation. The identification of the viscous Laplacian as the macroscopic shadow of the molecular Compton-coupling Brownian motion sourced from dx₄/dt = ic at every spacetime event is the McGucken-framework closure of the foundational question, developed in §§4.5, 13.3, and 14.3.6 of the present paper.

The identification established in this section, formalized as **Theorem 31** of §17A.9 below, is the following:

> *Each of the four open problems (I)–(IV) is a particular finite-mode instance of the same dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel / dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel dual structure descending from the foundational principle dx₄/dt = ic. The non-recognition of the Geometric Channel / Algebraic Channel duality by the four orthodox traditions has produced four parallel and structurally analogous open problems — each a finite-mode realization of the same Geometric Channel / Algebraic Channel non-recognition pattern in its respective domain, with tier-specific mathematical manifestations rather than literal identity across the four problems — for periods of sixty to two hundred years. The structural resolution under the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic supplies the foundational-geometric source for all four problems simultaneously.*

This is articulated at the **structural level ** of the present paper: a identification identifying the QM measurement problem, the NS smoothness-vs-blowup problem, the thermodynamics arrow-of-time question, and the dynamical-systems chaos-invariants problem as four expressions of the same Geometric Channel / Algebraic Channel non-recognition. ### §17A.2. The Historical Sequence 1824–1872: Thermodynamics Develops Without Relativity or Quantum Mechanics

The thermodynamic tradition developed entirely before the articulation of special relativity (Einstein 1905, Poincaré 1905, Minkowski 1908) and before the articulation of quantum mechanics (Heisenberg 1925, Schrödinger 1926). The foundational concepts of irreversibility, entropy, and the second law were forged in the period 1824–1872 — eighty-one years before special relativity and one hundred and one years before matrix mechanics — by physicists working entirely within the Newtonian framework supplemented by empirical thermodynamic observation. The temporal precedence of thermodynamics over relativity and quantum mechanics is the **first structural reason** the orthodox tradition has remained blind to the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel / dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel dual structure: the geometric content of the +ic-orientation of x₄ was not yet articulated when Boltzmann was working on the H-theorem, and the unification of statistical mechanics with relativity at the foundational-geometric level was never attempted by any orthodox-tradition figure.

**Carnot 1824.** Sadi Carnot's *Réflexions sur la puissance motrice du feu* [84] articulated the empirical irreversibility of heat engines and the impossibility of producing useful work from a single heat reservoir. The Carnot cycle established the maximum efficiency of any thermodynamic engine working between two heat reservoirs. The structural feature of Carnot's analysis: the irreversibility is **empirically observed** but **not foundationally explained**; the Newtonian framework available to Carnot does not contain any time-asymmetric element that could account for it.

**Clausius 1850 and 1865.** Rudolf Clausius in *Über die bewegende Kraft der Wärme* [85] formalized the Second Law of Thermodynamics as: *heat does not, of itself, pass from a body at lower temperature to one at higher temperature*. In 1865 [86] Clausius coined the term *entropy* (from Greek *τροπή*, "transformation"), denoted $S$, for the macroscopic quantity whose increase characterizes the irreversibility. Clausius wrote the famous summary: "*Die Energie der Welt ist constant. Die Entropie der Welt strebt einem Maximum zu.*" (*"The energy of the universe is constant. The entropy of the universe tends to a maximum."*) [86]. The structural feature: Clausius's $S$ is a macroscopic state-function whose existence is **postulated** to make the second law a definite mathematical statement; the foundational-geometric source of why $dS/dt \geq 0$ on the macroscopic scale despite time-reversible microscopic dynamics is **not addressed** by the 1850 or 1865 papers.

**Maxwell 1860, 1865, 1873.** James Clerk Maxwell established the kinetic theory of gases [131, 130], the foundations of classical electromagnetism [133], and articulated the *Maxwell demon* thought experiment [134] that already in 1867 (letter to Tait) and 1871 (Theory of Heat) raised the foundational question of whether the second law admits microscopic exceptions. The Maxwell demon — a hypothetical microscopic being that opens and closes a door between two gas chambers selectively to sort fast molecules to one side and slow to the other, thereby decreasing entropy without performing thermodynamic work — was Maxwell's articulation that the second law is *statistical*, not absolute. The structural feature: Maxwell already in the 1860s–1870s understood that the second law could not be a strict consequence of microscopic Newtonian mechanics, but he did not identify the foundational-geometric source of the macroscopic time-asymmetry.

**Boltzmann 1872: the H-theorem.** Ludwig Boltzmann in *Weitere Studien über das Wärmegleichgewicht unter Gasmolekülen* [87] published the H-theorem: starting from the Boltzmann transport equation $\partial_t f + v \cdot \nabla_x f = Q[f]$ where $Q[f]$ is the binary-collision integral and $f(x, v, t)$ is the one-particle distribution function on phase space, the H-functional
$$H(t) = \int f(x, v, t) \log f(x, v, t) \, dv \, dx$$
satisfies $dH/dt \leq 0$, equivalent under the identification $S = -k_B H$ to the second law $dS/dt \geq 0$. The derivation depends on the *Stosszahlansatz* (German: "collision-number ansatz") — the assumption that the pre-collision velocities of two molecules entering a binary collision are statistically uncorrelated, i.e., the joint distribution factorizes as $f_2(v_1, v_2) = f(v_1) f(v_2)$. The structural feature: Boltzmann derived dS/dt ≥ 0 from a kinetic-theory formalism that retains time-symmetric Newtonian mechanics for individual binary collisions, but the time-asymmetry is smuggled in through the Stosszahlansatz molecular-chaos assumption applied to pre-collision states only. The foundational-geometric source of why molecular chaos applies to pre-collision but not post-collision states remained unexplained.

**Loschmidt 1876: the reversibility objection.** Josef Loschmidt — Boltzmann's friend, former mentor, and lifelong colleague at the University of Vienna — in *Über den Zustand des Wärmegleichgewichtes eines Systems von Körpern mit Rücksicht auf die Schwerkraft* [88] raised the reversibility objection (published in the Sitzungsberichte der kaiserlichen Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Wien). The argument is purely structural and is articulated in the secondary literature [93, p. 14; 134, §3.2] verbatim as follows: if the H-theorem is taken as a strict mechanical consequence of Newtonian dynamics, and if for some trajectory of an isolated gas system the H-functional decreases monotonically from $t_0$ to $t_1$ to $t_2$, then by reversing all molecular velocities at $t_1$ one obtains an equally-valid Newtonian trajectory along which the H-functional must increase monotonically — and since the time-reversed initial state is an admissible Newtonian state of the same gas system, the H-theorem is structurally inconsistent with strict time-reversible Newtonian mechanics. Loschmidt's conclusion: no purely mechanical theorem deduced from time-reversible Newtonian dynamics can produce a time-asymmetric result. The structural feature: Loschmidt 1876 articulated the foundational obstruction precisely; he did not propose a resolution; and no resolution was forthcoming from Boltzmann or from the orthodox tradition that would identify a foundational-geometric source for the time-asymmetry.

**Boltzmann 1877: the statistical retreat.** Boltzmann's response, published in two papers [89, 88], retreated from the strict-theorem claim of 1872 to a statistical reinterpretation: $S = k_B \log W$, where $W$ is the multiplicity of microscopic configurations consistent with a given macroscopic state. The H-theorem is to be read as a statement that the H-functional decreases *with overwhelming statistical likelihood*, not as a strict theorem of Newtonian dynamics. The Loschmidt-reversed initial states are admissible but constitute a measure-zero set in phase space. The structural feature: the statistical retreat does not identify a foundational-geometric source for why the +t direction of time corresponds to states of overwhelming statistical likelihood and the -t direction does not; it pushes the foundational question onto the question of *initial conditions* (the Past Hypothesis of Albert 2000 [97]) and the *low-entropy initial state of the universe* (the Penrose Weyl Curvature Hypothesis [135, §27]).

The Boltzmann–Loschmidt episode of 1872–1877 articulated the foundational obstruction of orthodox statistical mechanics: the second law's time-asymmetry has no foundational-geometric source within Newtonian mechanics, and the orthodox response is a statistical retreat that pushes the unexplained content onto cosmological initial conditions. The McGucken-framework closure — that the +ic orientation of x₄'s expansion at every event supplies the foundational-geometric source from which dS/dt > 0 descends as a structural theorem [29, Theorem 9] — was unavailable to Boltzmann and to the orthodox tradition because the foundational principle dx₄/dt = ic had not yet been articulated.

**Burbury 1894, Bryan 1894.** Samuel Burbury [91] and George Bryan [92] independently identified the implicit time-asymmetry in the *Stosszahlansatz*: applied to pre-collision velocities the molecular-chaos assumption produces dH/dt ≤ 0; applied to post-collision velocities the same assumption produces dH/dt ≥ 0. The asymmetry of the H-theorem is structurally located in the *Stosszahlansatz*'s implicit choice of pre-collision rather than post-collision, not in the underlying Newtonian dynamics. This is the orthodox-literature confirmation that the second-law's time-asymmetry cannot be derived from time-symmetric microscopic dynamics without a foundational-geometric input. The orthodox tradition did not supply that foundational-geometric input; the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic supplies it as dx₄/dt = ic.

**Poincaré 1890: the recurrence theorem.** Henri Poincaré in *Sur le problème des trois corps et les équations de la dynamique* [137] established that a bounded Hamiltonian dynamical system returns arbitrarily close to its initial state in finite (though astronomically large) time. The Poincaré recurrence is a strict-theorem consequence of time-reversible Hamiltonian dynamics and is structurally inconsistent with strict monotone H-decrease over arbitrary times. The structural feature: Poincaré's recurrence is the strict-mathematical confirmation that strict time-asymmetric monotonicity of any function on a bounded Hamiltonian phase space is structurally impossible; the second law's time-asymmetry must be a finite-time statistical statement, not a strict-eternal theorem. The orthodox response: again, a retreat to *statistical* claims about *practical* observation timescales, not a foundational-geometric resolution.

**Gibbs 1902.** Josiah Willard Gibbs in *Elementary Principles in Statistical Mechanics* [138] formalized the canonical, microcanonical, and grand canonical ensembles and the dx₄/dt = ic framework of statistical-mechanical phase-space averages. The Gibbs entropy $S_G = -k_B \int \rho \log \rho \, d\Gamma$ on phase space supplies the orthodox bridge between microscopic and macroscopic. The structural feature: Gibbs's statistical mechanics is the orthodox-tradition framework within which the second law is *postulated as the maximization of $S_G$* under the constraints of conservation laws, but the foundational-geometric source of why the maximization principle holds is not derived within the Gibbs framework. It is taken as a postulate, or an "ergodic-hypothesis" assumption [139, 138], or a "typicality" argument [141, 140].

The thermodynamic and statistical-mechanical tradition of 1824–1902 thus articulated the empirical content of the second law, formalized its mathematical structure, encountered Loschmidt's foundational objection, retreated to a statistical reinterpretation, and identified the *Stosszahlansatz* time-asymmetry of Burbury–Bryan 1894, without at any point identifying a foundational-geometric source for the strict-positive entropy production at every spacetime event. The orthodox tradition's structural blindness here is **historically unavoidable**: special relativity was not articulated until 1905, the Wick rotation as a mathematical construct was not articulated until 1954, and the foundational principle dx₄/dt = ic was not articulated until McGucken 1998–99 [37, 73] with formal development beginning in 2024. The structural conditions for resolving the Loschmidt paradox via Geometric Channel identification as the +ic-projection of dx₄/dt = ic at every event simply did not exist within the orthodox tradition during the period in which the orthodox statistical-mechanical framework was being established.

### §17A.3. The Historical Sequence 1905–1908: Poincaré and Minkowski See x₄ = ict but Read It as Mathematical Formalism

The foundational principle dx₄/dt = ic states that the fourth dimension is expanding at velocity c spherically-symmetrically from every spacetime event, integrating to $x_4 = ict$ as a coordinate identity on the McGucken real four-manifold $\mathcal{M}_G$ [37, 39 Theorem 22.1, 48 Theorem 22.1]. The temporal sequence by which the orthodox tradition first encountered $x_4 = ict$ — Poincaré 1905–1906, Minkowski 1908 — and immediately classified it as *mathematical formalism* rather than as a physical statement about the geometry of spacetime is the **second structural reason** the orthodox tradition has remained blind to the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel / dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel dual structure for the past one hundred and sixteen years.

**Einstein 1905.** Albert Einstein in *Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper* [143] derived the Lorentz transformations from the two postulates (the principle of relativity and the constancy of c) and articulated the kinematics of special relativity in the real Minkowski metric form with $x_0 = ct$ (real coordinate). Einstein's 1905 paper does not use $x_4 = ict$. The structural feature of Einstein's 1905 treatment: the fourth coordinate is the real quantity $x_0 = ct$, the Minkowski metric is the indefinite-signature pseudo-Euclidean $ds^2 = -dx_0^2 + dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2$, and the time-coordinate is treated as a real geometric variable on the same footing as the spatial coordinates but with opposite signature.

**Poincaré 1905–1906.** Henri Poincaré in *Sur la dynamique de l'électron* [144, 143] derived the Lorentz transformations as a group-theoretic identity (the *Lorentz group*) and introduced the algebraic device of treating $ict$ as a fourth coordinate so that the Lorentz transformations become rotations of a four-dimensional space with a definite-signature Euclidean metric (after the $ict$ substitution). The structural feature: Poincaré 1905–1906 introduces $ict$ as an **algebraic device** to make the Lorentz transformations look like rotations in a Euclidean four-space. Poincaré does not assert that $ict$ corresponds to a physical entity expanding at velocity c spherically-symmetrically from every event; the use of $ict$ is presented as a mathematical convenience that simplifies the algebra of the Lorentz transformations and reveals their group-theoretic structure.

**Minkowski 1907 Göttingen lecture, 1908 Cologne lecture.** Hermann Minkowski's first lecture on relativity, *Das Relativitätsprinzip*, was given on 5 November 1907 to the Göttingen Mathematische Gesellschaft and published posthumously in 1915 [146]. Minkowski's celebrated *Raum und Zeit* lecture was given on 21 September 1908 at the 80th Assembly of German Natural Scientists and Physicians at Cologne and published in *Physikalische Zeitschrift* in 1909 [147]. The famous opening sentence of the Cologne lecture is verbatim:

> *"Meine Herren! Die Anschauungen über Raum und Zeit, die ich Ihnen entwickeln möchte, sind auf experimentell-physikalischem Boden erwachsen. Darin liegt ihre Stärke. Ihre Tendenz ist eine radikale. Von Stund' an sollen Raum für sich und Zeit für sich völlig zu Schatten herabsinken und nur noch eine Art Union der beiden soll Selbständigkeit bewahren."*

In Damour's 2008 translation [148]:

### §17A.4. The Historical Sequence 1925–1932: The Birth of Quantum Mechanics with the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel / dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel Dual Structure Articulated but Not Identified

The period 1925–1932 produced the foundational architecture of orthodox quantum mechanics: Heisenberg's matrix mechanics 1925 [155], Schrödinger's wave mechanics 1926 [100], Born's statistical interpretation 1926 [101], Heisenberg's uncertainty principle 1927 [102], Madelung's hydrodynamic formulation 1927 [156], and von Neumann's *Mathematische Grundlagen* 1932 [103]. In each case the orthodox tradition encountered the Geometric Channel / Algebraic Channel dual structure at the operational level — without recognizing it as a dual structure descending from a single foundational principle, and without identifying the foundational-geometric source of the Geometric Channel content. The temporal sequence in which each foundational figure encountered the dual structure, and the consequences for the orthodox-tradition non-recognition, are documented below.

**Heisenberg 1925, 1927.** Werner Heisenberg's *Über quantentheoretische Umdeutung kinematischer und mechanischer Beziehungen* [155] derived the matrix mechanics by replacing classical phase-space functions with non-commuting matrices. Heisenberg's 1927 paper *Über den anschaulichen Inhalt der quantentheoretischen Kinematik und Mechanik* [102] articulated the uncertainty relations $\Delta x \cdot \Delta p \geq \hbar/2$. The matrix-mechanics formulation already exhibits the dual structure: matrix operators (Algebraic Channel: algebraic content) act on state vectors, but the operational content of "measurement" is not specified within the matrix-mechanics framework. Heisenberg's 1927 uncertainty paper articulates the Geometric Channel content (probabilistic measurement) as a kinematical limit, not as a derivable consequence of the Algebraic Channel algebraic structure. The structural feature: Heisenberg 1925–1927 establishes that the algebraic and the probabilistic-measurement contents of quantum mechanics are not the same thing, but does not identify them as Geometric Channel and Algebraic Channel of a common foundational structure.

**Schrödinger 1926.** Erwin Schrödinger in *Quantisierung als Eigenwertproblem* [100] derived the time-dependent wave equation $i\hbar \, \partial_t \psi = H\psi$ where $H = -\hbar^2 \Delta / (2m) + V(x)$ is the Hamiltonian operator. The Schrödinger equation is **linear** (a linear differential equation in the wave function $\psi$), **deterministic** (the wave function at time $t$ is determined uniquely by the wave function at time $t_0$ via $\psi(t) = U(t-t_0) \psi(t_0)$ with $U(s) = \exp(-iHs/\hbar)$), **unitary** ($U(s) U(s)^\dagger = I$ preserves the $L^2$ norm of the wave function), and **time-reversible** (the equation $i\hbar \, \partial_t \psi = H\psi$ is invariant under the antiunitary transformation $\psi \to \bar\psi$, $t \to -t$). The structural feature: the Schrödinger equation supplies the **Algebraic Channel content** of quantum mechanics — the algebraic-symmetric-conservative-time-reversible content — but the equation itself is silent on how the wave function relates to observable measurement outcomes. The Geometric Channel content must be added separately.

**Born 1926.** Max Born in *Zur Quantenmechanik der Stoßvorgänge* [101] introduced the statistical interpretation of the wave function in a footnote that has become the most consequential footnote in the history of physics: the integral $\int_V |\psi(x)|^2 \, dx$ is the probability that a measurement of position localizes the particle in the region $V$. The Born rule is **non-linear** (the probability is the square of the amplitude, not the amplitude itself), **probabilistic** (the outcome of any individual measurement is not determined by the wave function), **non-unitary** (the act of measurement collapses the wave function to a single outcome, $\psi \to P_a \psi / \|P_a \psi\|$, which is not a unitary operation), and **time-asymmetric** (the post-measurement state cannot be uniquely inverted to reconstruct the pre-measurement state if the measurement is non-trivially projective). The structural feature: the Born rule supplies the **Geometric Channel content** of quantum mechanics — the geometric-projection-probabilistic-time-asymmetric content — but Born 1926 does not identify it as a Geometric Channel content descending from a single foundational principle that also generates the Algebraic Channel content. Born presents the rule as a postulate, not as a derivation.

**Madelung 1927: the closest the orthodox tradition came to recognizing Geometric Channel / Algebraic Channel.** Erwin Madelung in *Quantentheorie in hydrodynamischer Form* [156] published in *Zeitschrift für Physik* derived the equivalence between the Schrödinger equation and a pair of hydrodynamic equations. Writing the wave function in polar form $\psi(x, t) = R(x, t) \exp(iS(x, t)/\hbar)$ and substituting into the Schrödinger equation $i\hbar \, \partial_t \psi = -(\hbar^2/2m) \Delta \psi + V\psi$, Madelung obtained the *Madelung equations*:

$$\partial_t \rho + \nabla \cdot (\rho v) = 0$$
$$\partial_t v + (v \cdot \nabla) v = -\frac{1}{m} \nabla\left(V + Q\right)$$

with $\rho = R^2 = |\psi|^2$ (probability density), $v = (\nabla S)/m$ (probability-current velocity field), and $Q = -(\hbar^2/2m) (\Delta R)/R$ (the *quantum potential* or *Madelung potential*). The first equation is the continuity equation; the second is a hydrodynamic Euler-type equation with an additional quantum-potential force. The Madelung formulation reveals the dual structure of quantum mechanics in operational form: the system can be analyzed as a *probability fluid* with a *continuity-equation transport* (Algebraic Channel: continuous conservative-flow content, time-reversible) coupled to a *quantum-potential force* (Geometric Channel-like: the $\hbar^2$ content that has no classical analog and that vanishes in the $\hbar \to 0$ limit recovering classical mechanics).

The structural significance: Madelung 1927 articulated the dual structure of quantum mechanics in **hydrodynamic form** — the wave function reinterpreted as a probability-density fluid with a quantum-potential force — one hundred and seventy-two years after Euler 1755 [126] had articulated the dual structure of fluid dynamics in **inertial-plus-viscous form** (later completed by Navier 1822 [124] and Stokes 1845 [125]) and zero years after Born 1926 had articulated the dual structure of quantum mechanics in **algebraic-plus-projective form**. The Madelung equations are the explicit operational identification that quantum mechanics has a hydrodynamic Algebraic Channel content (continuity + Euler-type inertial-pressure dynamics) plus a quantum-potential Geometric Channel-like correction. **The orthodox tradition did not recognize the Madelung equations as articulating the Geometric Channel / Algebraic Channel dual structure descending from a foundational geometric principle**: Madelung 1927 itself treated the hydrodynamic formulation as an *analogy* useful for visualization, not as a identification. The orthodox response, summarized in the secondary literature [157, 156, 157, 158], has been to treat Madelung as a *mathematical curiosity*, with the pilot-wave-interpretation revival via Bohm 1952 [107] subsequently developing the hydrodynamic formulation as one possible interpretive structure rather than as the operational evidence of the Geometric Channel / Algebraic Channel duality.

The historical irony is structurally load-bearing: Madelung 1927 articulated the dual-channel hydrodynamic structure of QM **simultaneously** with Born 1926 articulating the Geometric Channel projective content, and yet the orthodox tradition has continuously failed to identify the operational equivalence between (i) Madelung's continuity equation + quantum potential and (ii) Born's projective measurement, both being Geometric Channel projections of the same algebraic Algebraic Channel wave-function content. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic's identification — that QM = Algebraic Channel wave function via Schrödinger + Geometric Channel projection via Born + dx₄/dt = ic at every event sourcing both — was structurally articulable in 1927 (the foundational principle dx₄/dt = ic was articulated by Wheeler-Princeton-influenced McGucken 1998–99 [37, 73] and formal-corpus 2024–present) **but was not articulated by the orthodox tradition** because the orthodox tradition's stance on $x_4 = ict$ as mathematical formalism (per §17A.3 above) precluded the foundational-geometric identification of the dual-channel structure as descending from the +ic-orientation of x₄.

**von Neumann 1932.** John von Neumann in *Mathematische Grundlagen der Quantenmechanik* [103] formalized quantum mechanics in the Hilbert-space framework and explicitly distinguished two types of state evolution. **Type I evolution** (von Neumann calls it *Prozess 2*): continuous unitary evolution $\psi(t) = U(t) \psi(0)$ with $U(t) = \exp(-iHt/\hbar)$, generated by the Schrödinger Hamiltonian, time-reversible, deterministic, unitary, preserving the $L^2$ norm and pure-state purity. **Type II evolution** (von Neumann calls it *Prozess 1*): discontinuous projective evolution $\psi \to P_a \psi / \|P_a \psi\|$ associated with the measurement of an observable, time-asymmetric, probabilistic (the outcome $a$ is selected according to the Born rule $p(a) = \|P_a \psi\|^2$), non-unitary, and irreversible. The structural feature: von Neumann 1932 **names the dual structure** at the operational level — he distinguishes two evolution types and acknowledges that they are structurally distinct — **but does not identify them as Geometric Channel and Algebraic Channel of a common foundational structure**. Von Neumann treats the existence of two evolution types as a foundational fact of quantum mechanics, with the foundational-geometric source of the asymmetry between Prozess 1 and Prozess 2 left unexplained. The von Neumann formulation of the quantum measurement problem — *why is the world structured such that two distinct evolution types are required to describe quantum systems?* — is the orthodox-tradition articulation of the Geometric Channel / Algebraic Channel dual structure without identification of its foundational source.

The structural significance of the 1925–1932 episode for the present argument: the orthodox tradition during the foundational period of quantum mechanics encountered the Geometric Channel / Algebraic Channel dual structure at four operational levels — Heisenberg's matrix-mechanics-versus-measurement asymmetry, Schrödinger's wave-equation-versus-Born-rule asymmetry, Madelung's continuity-equation-versus-quantum-potential structure, and von Neumann's Prozess-1-versus-Prozess-2 distinction — without identifying the four operational structures as instances of the same Geometric Channel / Algebraic Channel duality descending from the foundational principle dx₄/dt = ic. #### §17A.4bis.1. The von Neumann 1932 Statement: Verbatim Source and the Two Load-Bearing Claims

von Neumann's *Mathematische Grundlagen der Quantenmechanik* (Springer, Berlin, 1932; English translation by Robert T. Beyer, *Mathematical Foundations of Quantum Mechanics*, Princeton University Press, 1955) is the founding mathematical document of quantum mechanics — the Hilbert-space formalization that supplies the standard apparatus of the field. The Introductory Considerations of the 1932 book, before any technical content, contains the following statement on the relationship between macroscopic continuity and microscopic discreteness, verbatim per [vonNeumann1932MGQM, Introductory Considerations, pp. 3–4 of the Beyer 1955 English translation]:

> *"This is not the place to point out the great success which the quantum theory attained in the period from 1900 to 1925, a development which was dominated by the names of Planck, Einstein and Bohr. At the end of this period of development, it was clear beyond doubt that all elementary processes, i.e., all occurrences of an atomic or molecular order of magnitude, obey the 'discontinuous' laws of quanta. There were also available quantitative, quantum theoretical methods in almost all directions, which for the most part yielded results in good or at least fair agreement with experiment. And, what was fundamentally of greater significance, was that the general opinion in theoretical physics had accepted the idea that the principle of continuity ('natura non facit saltus'), prevailing in the macroscopic world, is merely simulated by an averaging process in a world which in truth is discontinuous by its very nature. This simulation is such that a man generally perceives the sum of many billions of elementary processes simultaneously, so that the leveling law of large numbers completely obscures the real nature of the individual processes."*

The passage contains two distinct load-bearing claims and one structural ranking:

**(vN-1) The macroscopic continuum as statistical illusion.** The principle of continuity ("natura non facit saltus") prevailing in the macroscopic world is, per von Neumann's verbatim formulation, **"merely simulated by an averaging process in a world which in truth is discontinuous by its very nature."** The continuum is not the foundational reality — it is the *appearance* produced by averaging over the discrete substrate. The discrete substrate is the foundational reality; the continuum is its statistical shadow.

**(vN-2) The leveling law obscures the foundational discreteness.** The mechanism by which the macroscopic continuum appears is articulated verbatim as: **"the leveling law of large numbers completely obscures the real nature of the individual processes."** The averaging across "many billions of elementary processes simultaneously" produces the continuum appearance; the underlying discrete processes are obscured but not eliminated. The leveling law is the *operational source* of the continuum illusion.

**(vN-3) The structural ranking — discreteness as foundationally more significant than the quantum methods themselves.** von Neumann ranks the discrete-substrate identification as **"fundamentally of greater significance"** than the quantitative quantum-theoretical methods developed by Planck (1900), Einstein (1905), and Bohr (1913) across the 1900–1925 period. The Planck–Einstein–Bohr methods produced quantitative agreement with experiment "in almost all directions," but the discrete-substrate identification underlying those methods is, per von Neumann, more important than the methods themselves. The 1932 ranking elevates the discrete-substrate position from a technical statement about atomic processes to a foundational claim about the universal nature of physical reality at all scales — including the macroscopic-fluid scale at which the Navier–Stokes equation operates.

##### §17A.4bis.6.1. The Verbatim Hilbert-Space Null-Element Postulate of 1932

The principal primary-source text for the second von Neumann anticipation is Chapter I §3 "Definition of Hilbert Space" of *Mathematische Grundlagen der Quantenmechanik* [vonNeumann1932MGQM] (English translation: Princeton University Press, 1955; reprint of the 2018 archive.org edition at *https://ia600101.us.archive.org/11/items/mathematical-foundations-of-quantum-mechanics-2018/Mathematical%20Foundations%20of%20Quantum%20Mechanics%202018.pdf*). The Hilbert-space axiomatization begins with the following postulate:

> **Postulate A** [vonNeumann1932MGQM, Chapter I §3, verbatim]: *"R is a linear space. That is: an addition $f + g$ and a 'scalar' multiplication $af$ are defined in R (for $f, g$ elements of R, $a$ a complex number: $f + g$ and $af$ belong to R), **and R has a null element**."*

The verbatim text appears in [264, §6.6.9.16.F, line 2904]. The phrase *"R has a null element"* is the structural primitive that the entire Hilbert-space axiomatization proceeds from. von Neumann then provides Footnote 38:

> **Footnote 38** [vonNeumann1932MGQM, Chapter I §3, verbatim, reproduced in [264, §6.6.9.16.F, line 2906]]: *"Besides the origin, or the null vector of R, there is also the number 0, so that the same symbol is used for two things. The relations are such, however, that no confusion should arise."*

von Neumann's Footnote 38 disambiguates his usage: the *null vector* of $R$ is identified with the *origin* of the linear space, distinct from the complex-number $0 \in \mathbb{C}$ used as a scalar multiplier. The structural role of the null vector is then made explicit at the very next theorem-grade content:

> **Definition 1** [vonNeumann1932MGQM, Chapter I §3, verbatim, reproduced in [264, §6.6.9.16.F, line 2908]]: *"The elements $f_1,.., f_k$ are linearly independent if it follows from $a_1 f_1 + \cdots + a_k f_k = 0$ ($a_1,.., a_k$ complex numbers) that $a_1 = \cdots = a_k = 0$."*

The vanishing of the linear combination *at the null vector* is the structural content of linear independence. The null vector is therefore not merely a placeholder element of the linear space; it is the *structural reference point* for the linear-independence content that the entire Hilbert-space construction relies on. Postulate A places this content at position one of the axiomatization — the very first structural commitment of the orthodox Hilbert-space framework that von Neumann codifies as the foundational mathematical apparatus of quantum mechanics.

### §17A.5. The Historical Sequence 1932–1963: Interpretive Struggle, Wick Rotation, and the Discovery of Deterministic Chaos

**Schrödinger 1935: the cat.** Erwin Schrödinger in *Die gegenwärtige Situation in der Quantenmechanik* [161] introduced the *Schrödinger-cat* thought experiment to articulate the operational difficulty of the measurement problem: if a quantum state can be a coherent superposition of microscopically-distinct states, the linear Type I evolution of the Schrödinger equation propagates the superposition to macroscopic objects (the cat being simultaneously alive and dead), and the Type II projective measurement is required to resolve the superposition into a definite outcome — but the boundary between Type I and Type II evolution is not specified by quantum mechanics itself. The structural feature: Schrödinger 1935 acknowledges that the orthodox-tradition framework does not contain a foundational specification of where Type I evolution ends and Type II evolution begins; the measurement problem is articulated as a structural incompleteness of the formalism.

**Einstein–Podolsky–Rosen 1935.** Albert Einstein, Boris Podolsky, and Nathan Rosen in *Can Quantum-Mechanical Description of Physical Reality Be Considered Complete?* [162] articulated the EPR thought experiment, demonstrating that strict-local quantum mechanics is structurally incompatible with strict-realism (the position taken by EPR that physical quantities have definite values independent of measurement). The structural feature: EPR articulates a non-locality-versus-realism choice that the orthodox tradition must make, with the further structural implication that the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel projective content is operationally non-local — the wave function collapses simultaneously over arbitrary spatial separations under the Type II projective evolution. Bell 1964 [163] later established the strict-mathematical impossibility of local-hidden-variable theories reproducing quantum-mechanical predictions, and the experimental confirmation of Bell-inequality violations by Aspect 1982 [164] and subsequent experiments [165] established the empirical non-locality of quantum mechanics. The McGucken-framework identification of the non-locality content as the +ic-projection of dx₄/dt = ic at every event was unavailable to the orthodox tradition.

**Wick 1954: the analytic-continuation device.** Gian-Carlo Wick in *Properties of Bethe-Salpeter Wave Functions* [154] published in *Physical Review* (volume 96, pages 1124–1134) introduced the analytic-continuation procedure now known as the *Wick rotation*. The verbatim abstract of [154] (verified from the *Physical Review* archive) is:

> *"A boundary condition at t = ±∞ (t being the 'relative' time variable) is obtained for the four-dimensional wave function of a two-body system in a bound state. It is shown that this condition implies that the wave function can be continued analytically to complex values of the 'relative time' variable; similarly the wave function in momentum space can be continued analytically to complex values of the 'relative energy' variable p₀. In particular one is allowed to consider the wave function for purely imaginary values of t, or respectively p₀, i.e., for real values of x₄ = ict and p₄ = ip₀. A wave equation satisfied by this function is obtained by rotation of the integration path in the complex plane of the variable p₀, and it is further shown that the formulation of the eigenvalue problem in terms of this equation presents several advantages in that many of the ordinary mathematical methods become available."*

The structural feature: Wick 1954 explicitly identifies $x_4 = ict$ — the same expression Minkowski used in 1907–1908 — and describes it as **the device by which the analytic continuation to imaginary time becomes available**, presenting it as a mathematical procedure useful because *"many of the ordinary mathematical methods become available"*. The Wick rotation is treated by Wick himself, and continuously by the orthodox quantum-field-theory tradition that has used it for seventy years (Euclidean field theory [166], lattice gauge theory [167], constructive quantum field theory [168, 167], Euclidean gravity [170, 169]), as a **mathematical analytic-continuation device**, not as a physical statement about the geometry of the fourth dimension. The orthodox-tradition phrase, *"Wick rotation as a useful mathematical trick"*, is the standard textbook articulation [172, p. 88; 171, §2.1; 172, §1.3].

The McGucken-framework identification — that $x_4 = ict$ is **not** a mathematical formalism device but is the integrated coordinate consequence of the physical fact dx₄/dt = ic, with the +ic orientation supplying the foundational-geometric source of Geometric Channel content across all four problem domains — is the **promotion of the Wick rotation from mathematical trick to physical theorem**, articulated formally in the McGucken-Wick rotation paper [39, Theorem 22.1; 48, Theorem 22.1]. This promotion has been continuously available to the orthodox tradition since 1954 — anyone reading Wick's 1954 paper could have asked the structural question *"what if x₄ = ict is not formalism but physical fact?"* — but no orthodox-tradition figure has asked this question or articulated this identification in the seventy-one years between 1954 and the present.

### §17A.6. The Historical Sequence 1970–2000: Decoherence Rises, the Measurement Problem Persists, and the Navier–Stokes Tradition Reaches Fefferman 2000

**Zeh 1970: the foundational decoherence paper.** H. Dieter Zeh in *On the Interpretation of Measurement in Quantum Theory* [109] published in *Foundations of Physics* introduced the decoherence concept: macroscopic quantum systems are not isolated; the interaction with the environment (the room's air, photons, phonons, etc.) produces rapid entanglement, and the off-diagonal density-matrix elements decay rapidly under the partial trace over the environment, producing an effective classical-statistical mixture at the level of the system alone. The structural feature: decoherence is presented as a derivation of Type II projective evolution from Type I unitary evolution of the system + environment, with the apparent Type II projection arising effectively from the loss of phase coherence under environment-tracing.

**Zurek 1981, 1991, 2003.** Wojciech Zurek in *Pointer Basis of Quantum Apparatus* [110], *Decoherence and the Transition from Quantum to Classical* [111], and *Decoherence, einselection, and the quantum origins of the classical* [112] developed the decoherence framework extensively. The Zurek einselection concept identifies the *preferred basis* (the pointer basis of a measurement device) as the basis that survives environment-induced decoherence. The structural feature: Zurek's framework explains *how* macroscopic classical behavior emerges from unitary microscopic dynamics — the off-diagonal density-matrix elements decay on the decoherence timescale, leaving an effective diagonal mixture in the pointer basis — but it does **not** explain *why* the universe contains an asymmetric arrow of time that selects the +t direction as the direction of decoherence (as opposed to the time-reversed -t direction along which the off-diagonal elements would re-cohere). The Zurek decoherence framework retains the Boltzmann–Loschmidt asymmetry: it explains macroscopic irreversibility in terms of microscopic Type I unitary evolution plus environmental tracing, but the foundational-geometric source of the +t-direction selection is not identified.

The orthodox-tradition literature on decoherence and the measurement problem [187, 186, 187, 188] continues to identify the unresolved structural issue: decoherence explains the appearance of macroscopic classicality but does not derive the Born-rule probabilities from the unitary evolution, and it does not identify the foundational-geometric source of the +t-direction selection. The orthodox tradition's persistent open questions, articulated in primary literature:

- **Bell 1990** in *Against "Measurement"* [113, p. 35–36, verbatim]: *"the result of solving the Schrödinger equation … is just a probability distribution for various observable consequences. One does not solve the Schrödinger equation to find out what is true."* Bell continues that *"the conventional formulation … is unprofessionally vague and ambiguous."*

- **Leggett 2005** in *The Quantum Measurement Problem* [114, p. 871, verbatim]: *"the orthodox quantum-mechanical description fails, in some sense or other, to describe physical reality."*

- **Weinberg 2017** in *The Trouble with Quantum Mechanics* [115, ¶3, verbatim]: *"I'm not as sure as I once was about the future of quantum mechanics. … perhaps the trouble lies not in quantum mechanics itself, but rather in the way it is interpreted."* Weinberg's structural diagnosis: *"the way I currently feel is that I am not satisfied with any of the existing interpretations of quantum mechanics."*

- **Penrose 2004** in *The Road to Reality* [135, §29.2, p. 786, verbatim]: *"there is undoubtedly something missing from current quantum theory. … R [the reduction process, Type II evolution] is fundamentally different from U [the unitary evolution, Type I evolution] in being non-linear, time-asymmetric, and discontinuous. … The combined behaviour appears, when taken together, to involve a sort of inconsistency."*

### §17A.7. The Four Orthodox "Contradictions" in the Measurement Problem, Sourced to Primary Literature, and Their dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel / dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel Identification

The orthodox literature contains four standard "contradictions" or "apparent paradoxes" articulated in the measurement-problem literature, each of which is, under the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, a Geometric Channel / Algebraic Channel signature rather than a structural contradiction. The four are sourced verbatim or paraphrased from primary orthodox-literature articulations below.

**Orthodox contradiction (i): "Quantum mechanics is deterministic but probabilistic."** The orthodox-tradition articulation is found in standard textbooks and review articles. Dirac 1930 in *The Principles of Quantum Mechanics* [196, §27, verbatim]: *"the wave equation has a precise and definite form in terms of the variables defining the dynamical system, and given the wave function at any time it determines uniquely the wave function at any later time. … But [the wave function] determines only the probabilities of the different outcomes of an observation."* The Dirac articulation makes the operational point precisely: the wave function's *time-evolution* (Algebraic Channel content via Schrödinger) is deterministic, while the wave function's *operational meaning under measurement* (Geometric Channel content via Born) is probabilistic. The orthodox tradition treats this as an apparent contradiction requiring interpretation; the McGucken-framework identification is that the Algebraic Channel content (deterministic unitary evolution) and the Geometric Channel content (probabilistic projective measurement) are the two functorial images of the foundational principle dx₄/dt = ic at every event. There is no contradiction; there are two channels with different functorial structures.

**Orthodox contradiction (ii): "Quantum mechanics is reversible but measurement is irreversible."** The orthodox-tradition articulation is found in Penrose 2004 [135, §29.2, verbatim] (quoted above) and Wheeler–Zurek 1983 [197, p. 5, verbatim]: *"the Schrödinger equation is invariant under time reversal, but the measurement process appears to introduce an irreversible step into the description."* The Wheeler–Zurek articulation makes the operational point: the Schrödinger evolution (Algebraic Channel content) is time-reversal-invariant, while the projective measurement (Geometric Channel content) is operationally time-asymmetric (the post-measurement state cannot be uniquely inverted to reconstruct the pre-measurement state). The orthodox tradition treats this as an apparent contradiction; the McGucken-framework identification is that Algebraic Channel (the time-symmetric Hamiltonian content) and Geometric Channel (the +ic-oriented x₄ content producing the operational asymmetry) are the two functorial images of the foundational principle dx₄/dt = ic. The asymmetry between the channels is the structural fact that the +ic orientation of x₄'s expansion is the foundational source of the Geometric Channel content per [42, Theorem 80]; the appearance of contradiction under the orthodox single-channel reading dissolves under the dual-channel identification.

**Orthodox contradiction (iii): "Quantum mechanics is linear but the Born rule is non-linear."** The orthodox-tradition articulation is found in Wigner 1963 in *The Problem of Measurement* [198, p. 5, verbatim]: *"the Schrödinger equation is a linear equation in the wave function, but the Born interpretation requires the square of the absolute value of the wave function, which is non-linear in the wave function."* The Wigner articulation makes the operational point: the Schrödinger evolution (Algebraic Channel content) is linear in $\psi$, while the Born rule $p(a) = |\langle a | \psi \rangle|^2$ (Geometric Channel content) is quadratic in $\psi$. The orthodox tradition treats this as an apparent contradiction; the McGucken-framework identification is that the linear Algebraic Channel content (the algebraic-functor reading) and the quadratic Geometric Channel content (the geometric-functor reading via Sphere projection to the spatial-projection probability density) are functorial images at different positions in the foundational structure descending from dx₄/dt = ic.
