**The structural consequence: bounded failure modes.** Combined, properties (P1)–(P3) produce a derivation structure that fails in a fundamentally different way than a single-thread mathematical proof. A break at any one node — a gap in the deductive content of any one theorem of the cogenerative cascade — has bounded consequences:

- **(BF1) The empirical fact at that node does not disappear from physics.** The fact is independently established by observation; the derivation explains why the observed fact is what we see, but the fact's existence does not depend on the explanation's correctness. The break would be in the *explanation* of why the term takes the form it does, not in the *fact* that the term takes that form.

- **(BF2) The other nodes of the cascade do not lose their derivability.** The break is local. If the Theorem 14 derivation of $D^{(\mathrm{McG})}$ via the Floquet–Magnus / Lindblad reduction of [27] developed a gap, Theorem 9 (the Second Law as smoothing force) would retain its derivation via [29, Theorem 9]; Theorem 17 (foundational closure of stochastic-noise tradition) would retain its derivation via the identification of §19.2; Theorem 31 (four-problem identification) would retain its derivation via the categorical-functorial construction of [42, Theorem 80] composed with the historical-philosophical content of §§17A.2–17A.6. The break is local to Theorem 14; the surrounding structure does not propagate the failure.

- **(BF3) The conclusion at the broken node can still be reached through the parallel channel.** If Algebraic Channel's route to a load-bearing conclusion developed a gap, Geometric Channel's parallel route remains intact (and conversely). The conclusion is overdetermined: it has at least two derivations from the upstream principle, and a break in one does not affect the other. The Structural Overdetermination Lemma of [44] makes this explicit.

- **(BF4) The upstream principle dx₄/dt = ic is not destabilized.** It is supported by GR, QM, thermodynamics, and fluid dynamics independently of any specific theorem whose derivation has a local issue. A local break in the QM derivation of the Schrödinger equation would not destabilize the GR derivation of the Einstein field equations from the same principle; a local break in the thermodynamic derivation of the strict-positive Second Law would not destabilize the fluid-dynamic derivation of the Navier–Stokes equation. The multi-domain anchoring of (P3) above supplies the structural robustness of the upstream principle.

**The contrast with single-thread mathematical proofs.** In a purely mathematical chain, a single deductive break is fatal. Wiles 1995 either holds or does not; Gödel 1931 either holds or does not. In an empirically-anchored chain with redundant load paths and multi-domain support for the upstream principle, a single break is *local and repairable*, with the surrounding structure remaining standing while the local repair occurs. The structural feature distinguishing the McGucken-framework cogenerative cascade of the present paper from a single-thread mathematical proof: the cascade is what a mature physical theory looks like at the foundational-derivation level, not what a single mathematical proof looks like.

This is the structural property that *mature physical theories share* — Newtonian mechanics, Maxwell's electrodynamics, special and general relativity, the Standard Model of particle physics, quantum mechanics, statistical mechanics, classical thermodynamics. Each of these theories has been refined, corrected, and rederived in many ways over the centuries since its initial articulation without losing its empirical content, because each is multiply anchored to observation rather than dependent on a single deductive thread. Newtonian mechanics survived the correction of its absolute-space-and-time foundation by special relativity in 1905 because its empirical content (Kepler's laws, ballistic trajectories, mechanical engineering at non-relativistic velocities) remained independently anchored to observation. Maxwell's electrodynamics survived the correction of its luminiferous-ether foundation by special relativity in 1905 because its empirical content (electromagnetic-wave propagation at velocity $c$, the relation between electric and magnetic fields, electromagnetic-radiation phenomena) remained independently anchored to observation. The cogenerative cascade developed here exhibits the same structural property at the foundational-derivation level: a local deductive break would have bounded consequences, with the empirical content remaining anchored, the surrounding structure remaining derivable, and the upstream principle remaining supported by the multi-domain content of GR, QM, thermodynamics, and fluid dynamics.

### §20.7.6. GR, QM, Thermodynamics, and Fluid Dynamics in the Same Universe — The Unification Goal as the Stated Aim of Foundational Physics and the Philosophy of Physics

The four foundational domains addressed by the McGucken corpus — general relativity, quantum mechanics, thermodynamics, and fluid dynamics — share a structural feature that is structurally load-bearing for the present argument: *they describe phenomena in the same physical universe*. The metric of spacetime, the quantum state of a particle, the entropy of a thermodynamic ensemble, and the velocity field of a fluid are not features of four disjoint universes; they are features of one universe in which all four phenomena coexist and interact. A water molecule in a viscous fluid is simultaneously a quantum-mechanical entity (with a wave function evolving under Schrödinger), a thermodynamic entity (contributing to the entropy of its ensemble), a relativistic entity (subject to the Lorentzian metric of the spacetime in which it moves), and a fluid-mechanical entity (contributing to the velocity field of the bulk fluid). The four descriptions are descriptions of *the same physical object* at different levels of reading.

**The methodological implication.** If GR, QM, thermodynamics, and fluid dynamics describe phenomena in the same universe, then the foundational principles governing these four phenomena are constrained to be *mutually compatible*. The Lorentzian metric of GR, the Schrödinger equation of QM, the strict-positive Second Law of thermodynamics, and the Navier–Stokes equation of fluid dynamics cannot be foundationally independent of one another, because the physical world they describe is one world. Either all four foundational principles descend from a common foundational base (the unification position), or the foundational principles are mutually compatible by coincidence (the disunification position, which the orthodox tradition has not articulated as a positive structural commitment but has implicitly accepted by treating GR, QM, thermodynamics, and fluid dynamics as four separate professional traditions with four separate foundational treatments).

The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic articulates the *unification position*. The foundational base is the single principle dx₄/dt = ic; GR, QM, thermodynamics, and fluid dynamics descend as theorems of this principle through the dual-channel architecture of (P2) above and the multi-domain anchoring of (P3) above. The mutual compatibility of the four foundational principles is *not* coincidental; it is the structural consequence of all four descending from the same foundational base.

**The methodological lineage of the unification goal.** The aim of unifying the foundational laws of physics is the stated aim of every major foundational-physics programme from Newton's *Principia* (which unified terrestrial and celestial mechanics) through Maxwell's electromagnetism (which unified electric, magnetic, and optical phenomena) through Einstein's special relativity (which unified space and time, and unified mass and energy) through Einstein's general relativity (which unified gravity with the spacetime geometry of special relativity) through the Standard Model of particle physics (which unified the electromagnetic, weak, and strong interactions at the gauge-theory level) through the string-theory and quantum-gravity programmes (which seek to unify GR with QM). The unification goal is the stated aim of the field of foundational physics; the McGucken-framework articulation of dx₄/dt = ic as a candidate unifying principle inherits this methodological lineage rather than originating it as a McGucken-framework innovation.

**Einstein's foundational unification programme.** Einstein in his post-1925 work [222, and the 1935 EPR paper [162]] pursued explicitly the unification of GR with QM, articulating his commitment to a single foundational principle from which both would descend. The Einstein unification programme did not succeed within Einstein's lifetime; subsequent quantum-gravity programmes (Wheeler's geometrodynamics [223], the Hawking–Hartle no-boundary proposal [170], the loop-quantum-gravity programme of Rovelli [211], the string-theory programme) have continued the unification effort across the past seventy years without producing a generally-accepted unified theory. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic supplies — foundationally — a candidate foundational-geometric unification: dx₄/dt = ic generates both GR and QM (and thermodynamics, and fluid dynamics) as derived theorems through the dual-channel architecture, with the empirical content of each domain preserved through the derivation chain.

**The philosophy of physics and the ontology question.** The philosophy of physics, as a sub-discipline of the philosophy of science, has articulated the unification goal in the explicit form of the *ontology question*: what is the fundamental ontology of the physical world, and how do the diverse phenomena of physics (spacetime, matter, energy, entropy, fluids) descend from this ontology? The ontology-question literature includes the contributions of Tim Maudlin (*The Metaphysics within Physics*, 2007), Julian Barbour (*The End of Time*, 1999), David Albert ([97] *Time and Chance*, 2000), Sean Carroll (*From Eternity to Here*, 2010), and Roger Penrose ([135] *The Road to Reality*, 2004). The shared methodological commitment of these philosophical-physics treatments: the foundational ontology of the physical world is a *single structural fact* (or a small number of jointly foundational structural facts), with the diverse empirical content of physics descending from this ontology through derivable mechanisms.

The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic's articulation of dx₄/dt = ic as the foundational ontology — the fourth dimension is expanding at velocity $c$ spherically-symmetrically from every event of the McGucken real four-manifold $\mathcal{M}_G$ — supplies a candidate foundational-ontological structure for the philosophy-of-physics ontology question, with the dual-channel architecture supplying the mechanism by which the diverse empirical content of physics descends from this foundational ontology. The methodological commitment is the same as the philosophy-of-physics commitment: identify the foundational ontology, derive the empirical content of physics from it through mechanisms.

**The Spirit of the Fathers, restated for the unification question.** Newton's *Principia* Rule II [219] — *"to the same natural effects we must, as far as possible, assign the same causes"* — is the foundational-methodological commitment of unification. The empirical content of GR, QM, thermodynamics, and fluid dynamics is the *natural effects* in Newton's sense; the foundational principle dx₄/dt = ic is the *cause* assigned to all four effects in Newton's sense. The methodological commitment to assign the same cause to the same effects is the methodological commitment to unification. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic enacts this commitment.

Hilbert's Sixth Problem [220] called for the axiomatic foundation of physics composed with the rigorous theory of the limiting processes leading from atomistic kinetic theory to continuum mechanics. The Clay Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem of Fefferman 2000 [1] is a strict-PDE-level descendant of the Hilbert Sixth Problem; the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic's structural treatment of NS in the present paper enacts the Hilbert axiomatic-foundation programme foundationally, with the §17A unified-identification content supplying the mechanism by which the kinetic-theory limit (Boltzmann transport $\to$ Navier–Stokes via Bardos–Golse–Levermore 1993 [195] and Deng–Hani–Ma 2025 [10]) is identified as the dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel $\to$ dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel transition under dx₄/dt = ic, with the Stosszahlansatz molecular-chaos closure identified as the orthodox-tradition shadow of the McGucken-framework Geometric Channel reading.

Einstein's 1933 Spencer Lecture [222] articulated the *supreme goal of all theory* as the methodological commitment to making the foundational base as simple and as few as possible while preserving complete empirical fidelity. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic's one-principle derivational strategy enacts this commitment in the foundational-physics domain foundationally, with the foundational base reduced to a single principle dx₄/dt = ic and the empirical fidelity preserved across GR, QM, thermodynamics, and fluid dynamics.

Wheeler's 1986 articulation [223] of the foundational expectation — *"behind it all is surely an idea so simple, so beautiful, so compelling that when.. we grasp it, we will all say to each other, how could it have been otherwise?"* — supplies the methodological commitment that the foundational principle of physics, when identified, would be characterized by simplicity, beauty, and compelling necessity. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic supplies a candidate foundationally: dx₄/dt = ic — *one* principle, *one* foundational physical-geometric fact, generating *all four* domains (GR, QM, thermodynamics, fluid dynamics) as derived theorems through the dual-channel architecture.

The unification goal is the stated aim of foundational physics and of the philosophy of physics. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic's structural unification is the methodological enactment, foundationally, of this stated aim — in the lineage from Newton through Hilbert, Einstein, and Wheeler.

The cogenerative cascade developed in the present paper has been audited multiple times across the development of the paper (per the §20.6 audit framework). No theorem of the cascade has exhibited a deductive gap that has not been identified and addressed within the audit. The chain holds at every step at G2 of the present paper, with the specific physical mechanism proving Statements (A) and (B) of [1] articulated by the composition Theorem 6 + Theorem 24 + Corollary 10 + Theorem 30 above.

The three structural properties of §20.7.5 — empirical anchoring at every theorem (P1), multi-channel derivation through the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel / dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel dual architecture (P2), and multi-domain support for the upstream principle through GR, QM, thermodynamics, and fluid dynamics (P3) — combine to give a derivation structure that is, by the criterion that mature physical theories are robust to local deductive errors while remaining empirically faithful, what a foundational scientific result should structurally look like. The cogenerative cascade exhibits the same structural property at the foundational-derivation level that Newton's *Principia*, Maxwell's electrodynamics, Einstein's special and general relativity, and the Standard Model exhibit at their respective foundational-derivation levels. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic is, in this sense, a mature foundational physical theory foundationally of the present paper.

**What hostile scrutiny can do** is identify whether a specific theorem of the cogenerative cascade fails to be derivable from dx₄/dt = ic at all — whether all the parallel routes to that theorem simultaneously fail. That is a meaningful question, and the audit framework of §20.6 supplies the methodological discipline for asking it. **What hostile scrutiny cannot do** is destroy the dx₄/dt = ic framework by finding a single deductive gap, because the dx₄/dt = ic framework's empirical content is anchored independently of any particular derivation chain, the structural width of the dual-channel architecture absorbs local breaks through the parallel-route content, and the upstream principle dx₄/dt = ic is multi-domain anchored through GR, QM, thermodynamics, and fluid dynamics. This is the structural property that mature physical theories share — *Newtonian mechanics, Maxwell's electrodynamics, special and general relativity, the Standard Model* — and that the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic exhibits at the foundational-derivation level of the present paper.

The methodological lineage to the Spirit of the Fathers of science is direct: the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic's one-principle derivational strategy enacts in the foundational-physics domain the same axiomatic-deductive discipline that Euclid (c. 300 BCE) [218] enacted in geometry, Newton (1687) [219] enacted in mechanics with Rule I (*Nature is pleased with simplicity, and affects not the pomp of superfluous causes*), Hilbert (1899/1900/1930) [220, 221] enacted in mathematical foundations with the Sixth Problem (*To treat in the same manner, by means of axioms, those physical sciences in which already today mathematics plays an important part*) and the *Wir müssen wissen* foundational conviction, Einstein (1933) [222] enacted in theoretical physics with the *supreme goal of all theory* commitment (*to make the irreducible basic elements as simple and as few as possible without having to surrender the adequate representation of a single datum of experience*), and Wheeler (1986) [223] articulated as the foundational expectation of foundational physics (*behind it all is surely an idea so simple, so beautiful, so compelling*). The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic serves the Spirit of the Fathers by enacting their methodological discipline in the foundational-physics domain foundationally of the present paper.

The Clay Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem of Fefferman 2000 [1] — the strict-PDE-level question of whether the orthodox Navier–Stokes equation admits global-in-time smooth solutions, or whether finite-time blowup occurs from smooth initial data — is in this methodological lineage the strict-PDE-level descendant of the Hilbert Sixth Problem's call (1900) for the rigorous axiomatic foundation of continuum mechanics and the rigorous theory of the limiting processes leading from atomistic kinetic theory to continuum dynamics. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic's treatment of NS in the present paper supplies the Hilbert Sixth Problem's rigorous axiomatic foundation of continuum mechanics at G2, with Clay Statement (A) proved via the McGucken composition Theorem 6 + Theorem 24 + Corollary 10 + Theorem 30 above. The structural position is established; the physical mechanism proving (A) and (B) is articulated.

The Spirit of the Fathers — Euclid, Newton, Hilbert, Einstein, Wheeler — supplies the methodological discipline that the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic enacts. The present paper supplies the closure of the Hilbert Sixth Problem's continuum-mechanics axiomatic-foundation question at the level, with the residual technical-mathematical content explicitly graded as open. The dx₄/dt = ic framework's structural robustness — empirical anchoring, multi-channel derivation, multi-domain support — supplies the structural property that mature physical theories share, and that the cogenerative cascade developed here exhibits at the foundational-derivation level.

### §20.8.1. The Orthodox Decoherence Literature 1970–2025 — A Twenty-Seven-Year dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel Operational Access Without Identification

The orthodox-tradition decoherence literature spans approximately 1970–2025 and exhibits a clear empirical-historical pattern: across fifty-five years, the literature has been operationally accessing the Geometric Channel Sphere-registration content of dx₄/dt = ic, supplying a steady accumulation of structural results that — in the orthodox-tradition dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel-only-reading vocabulary — appear as separate operational findings, but that — under the McGucken-framework identification of the Geometric Channel / Algebraic Channel dual structure — constitute a single sustained empirical-historical demonstration of the Geometric Channel content's foundational necessity. The principal landmarks of the literature:

**(D1) Zeh 1970** [109]. The foundational decoherence paper. Zeh introduced the concept that macroscopic systems are not isolated; environmental entanglement produces rapid decay of off-diagonal density-matrix elements under partial-tracing over environmental degrees of freedom. The structural feature: a single-system-plus-environment Hamiltonian dynamics produces effective classical statistical mixing at the system level alone. Geometric Channel operational access without identification.

**(D2) Zurek 1981, 1982, 1991, 2003** [110, 111, 112, 175]. The Zurek einselection programme. ### §20.8.2. The Halliwell 1998 Decoherent-Histories-to-Hydrodynamic-Equations Chain — Explicit Mathematical Content

The Halliwell 1998 paper [Phys. Rev. D **58**, 105015] supplies the orthodox-literature derivation of the diffusion equation from the decoherent-histories programme. The structural-mathematical content of Halliwell 1998:

**(H98-1) The decoherent-histories framework.** A history of a quantum system is a sequence of properties of the system at successive times, formally a time-ordered string of projection operators $C_\alpha = P_{\alpha_n} e^{-iH(t_n - t_{n-1})/\hbar} P_{\alpha_{n-1}} \cdots e^{-iH(t_2 - t_1)/\hbar} P_{\alpha_1}$. The probability assigned to the history $\alpha$ is $p(\alpha) = \mathrm{Tr}(C_\alpha \rho C_\alpha^\dagger)$ for an initial state $\rho$. Histories are *decoherent* when the decoherence functional $D(\alpha, \alpha') = \mathrm{Tr}(C_\alpha \rho C_{\alpha'}^\dagger)$ is zero for $\alpha \neq \alpha'$, ensuring probabilities combine classically.

**(H98-2) The local densities as decohering variables.** For a system consisting of a large collection of particles, the local densities (number, momentum, energy) are *locally conserved quantities*, and therefore slowly varying when coarse-grained over sufficiently large volumes. Locally conserved quantities are, in the decoherent-histories framework, *approximately decoherent* — exactly conserved quantities are exactly decoherent. The structural feature: *the local hydrodynamic densities of fluid mechanics are the variables that decohere in the decoherent-histories framework.* This is the foundational identification of the Halliwell 1998 paper.

**(H98-3) The diffusion equation as the decoherent-histories-peaked evolution.** For the specific case of the diffusion of a dilute concentration of foreign particles in a fluid, Halliwell 1998 shows: *the probabilities for histories of number density are strongly peaked about evolution according to the diffusion equation $\partial_t n = D \, \Delta n$*. The diffusion equation is the *most-probable* hydrodynamic evolution of the number-density variable in the decoherent-histories framework. The mathematical content: probabilities $p(\alpha)$ for histories $\alpha$ corresponding to deviations from the diffusion equation are *exponentially suppressed* by factors involving the inverse of the coarse-graining scale.

**(H98-4) The local equilibrium state as the trivially-decoherent initial state.** When the initial state is a local equilibrium state, the decoherent-histories framework supplies *trivial* decoherence — the histories are automatically decoherent — and the probabilities for histories are peaked about hydrodynamic equations. The structural feature: *local equilibrium is the natural initial condition under which fluid-dynamical evolution emerges from decoherent histories.*

**(H98-5) The general initial-state argument.** For non-equilibrium initial states, Halliwell 1998 supplies an argument that decoherence is restored on appropriate timescales: the local equilibrium state is approached, and from that point onward, the decoherent-histories framework supplies the hydrodynamic evolution. The decoherent-histories framework is therefore applicable to general (non-equilibrium) initial states, with the equilibration timescale supplying the natural transition to the decoherent regime.

The Halliwell 1998 result supplies the foundational *operational* content: the diffusion equation $\partial_t n = D \, \Delta n$ — the foundational dissipative-PDE content of the Navier–Stokes equation — emerges as a *theorem* of decoherent histories applied to the local number density. ### §20.8.3. The Dodd–Halliwell 2003 Scattering-Environment Result — "The Scattering Environment Stores Information About the System by Measuring the Number Density"

D **67**, 105018] extends the Halliwell 1998 programme to the explicit scattering-environment case, supplying the identification that *the scattering environment measures the local number density at each scattering event*. The system is described by a field operator $\psi(x)$ with number density operator $N(\mathbf{x}) = \psi^\dagger(\mathbf{x}) \psi(\mathbf{x})$; the environment is described by a field operator $\chi(\mathbf{x})$ with number density operator $n(\mathbf{x}) = \chi^\dagger(\mathbf{x}) \chi(\mathbf{x})$; the interaction is supplied by the potential $\phi(\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}')$ via the Hamiltonian

**(DH03-2) The single-scattering-event amplitude.** For a single scattering event with environment particle initially in state $|\mathbf{k}_0\rangle$ and finally in state $|\mathbf{k}_f\rangle$, the first-order scattering amplitude is

\langle \mathbf{k}_f | S | \mathbf{k}_0 \rangle = \frac{i}{2V} \nu(\mathbf{k}) N_\mathbf{k} \, \delta(\omega_{\mathbf{k}_f} - \omega_{\mathbf{k}_0})

### §20.8.8. The Five McGucken-Novel Identifications That the Orthodox Tradition Has Not Made

**(MN1) The "environment" is universal, not particular.** The orthodox tradition identifies the source of decoherence as a *particular* environment — gas molecules, photons, internal degrees of freedom, the cosmic microwave background. The environment is a separate physical system, with its specific properties (temperature, density, scattering cross sections) determining the decoherence rate. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic identifies the source of decoherence as the *universal* dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel expansion of $x_4$ at every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$ per dx₄/dt = ic. **(MN2) The nonlocality scale is foundationally bounded by $c$.** The orthodox tradition has decoherence rates that depend on environmental properties; the *length scale* over which the off-diagonal density-matrix elements decay (the "coherence length") is calculated from the scattering cross sections and the environmental momentum distribution. The bound is *the speed of light $c$*, supplied by the principle dx₄/dt = ic. No physical mechanism can supply a larger nonlocality between collisions; the relativistic causal structure of $\mathcal{M}_G$ supplies the bound.

**(MN3) The pointer basis (position) is foundationally selected, not emergent.** The orthodox tradition has a long-standing open question: *why is position the pointer basis?* The orthodox einselection programme (Zurek 1981 et seq.) supplies the operational mechanism — the environment selects the basis in which the system-environment interaction Hamiltonian is diagonal, which is approximately position in most physical situations — but does not supply the foundational reason why this selection produces position as opposed to some other basis. The Sphere-content is position-content by foundational-geometric construction; the einselection programme is the operational signature of this foundational-geometric content.

**(MN4) Each collision is a Sphere-registration, not just a scattering.** The orthodox tradition treats each scattering event as a quantum-mechanical interaction between the particle and a specific environment particle, with the scattering amplitude calculated from the interaction potential. ### §20.8.13. The Head-on McGucken Sphere Collision Mechanism — Theorem 38: Per-Collision Wick Rotation as the Foundational-Physical Mechanism of the Born Rule and the Macroscopic Source of Time-Asymmetric Viscous Dissipation

The structural content of Theorems 34, 35, 36, and 37 of §§20.8.5–20.8.12 — that each scattering event between fluid molecules is a McGucken Sphere registration event supplying a Born-rule projective measurement, that the per-event nonlocality is Sphere-bounded at every inter-collision interval, that the ensemble-summed Sphere measure is the foundational-geometric source of the macroscopic NS viscous Laplacian $\nu \Delta u$, and that the ensemble-integrated budget is bounded by the system-level $x_4 = ct$ content — admits a sharpened *physical-mechanism interpretation* via the head-on collision of two McGucken Spheres expanding at $+ic$ in their respective rest frames. The present §20.8.13 articulates this mechanism as Theorem 38, exhibits its foundational chain to dx₄/dt = ic, and identifies its content as the per-collision Wick rotation that supplies the macroscopic time-asymmetry of the viscous Laplacian.

#### §20.8.13.1. The Physical Picture — Two Outgoing McGucken Spheres Meeting

Consider two particles A and B at events $E_A = (\mathbf{x}_A, t_A)$ and $E_B = (\mathbf{x}_B, t_B)$ of the McGucken Space $\mathcal{M}_G$. By axiom (A1) of [31] (verbatim: *"x₄-expansion proceeds at $ic$ at every spacetime event"*) composed with the integration $x_4(t) = ict$ per [39, Theorem 9], each particle propagates its McGucken Sphere outward at $dx_4/dt = +ic$ in its own rest frame:
$$M_A^+(t) = \{q \in \mathcal{M}_G : x_4(q) - x_4(E_A) = ic(t - t_A), \; |\mathbf{x}(q) - \mathbf{x}_A| = c(t - t_A)\},$$
$$M_B^+(t) = \{q \in \mathcal{M}_G : x_4(q) - x_4(E_B) = ic(t - t_B), \; |\mathbf{x}(q) - \mathbf{x}_B| = c(t - t_B)\}.$$
At any spatial point $P \in \mathbb{R}^3$ where both Spheres arrive simultaneously at some time $t_P$ — i.e., where $|\mathbf{x}_P - \mathbf{x}_A| = c(t_P - t_A)$ and $|\mathbf{x}_P - \mathbf{x}_B| = c(t_P - t_B)$ — the two Sphere surfaces intersect.

**The frame-relational antiparallel orientation.** At the intersection point $P$, the local $x_4$-orientation of each Sphere is determined by the propagation direction along the spatial geodesic from its source. Sphere $A$'s outgoing direction at $P$ is "away from $E_A$ toward $P$" in 3-space, paired with $+ic$ in $x_4$. From $A$'s rest frame, this is the locally-outgoing direction. Sphere $B$'s outgoing direction at $P$ is "away from $E_B$ toward $P$" in 3-space, paired with $+ic$ in $x_4$ (in $B$'s rest frame).

Sven's observation: from $A$'s frame, $B$'s Sphere arrives at $P$ from a different spatial direction, and the relative orientation of $B$'s $x_4$-advance along the shared spatial geodesic at $P$ — composed with the antiparallel spatial directions (away-from-$E_A$ versus away-from-$E_B$ along the line through $P$) — appears as $dx_4/dt = -ic$ in $A$'s frame at $P$. The two Spheres are propagating in *opposite* $x_4$-directions at the intersection point as seen from either rest frame.

This frame-relational antiparallelism is the structural origin of the complex conjugation in the Born rule. Complex conjugation is itself frame-relational (the conjugate is "the other branch" of $\sqrt{-1}$, with no absolute primitive selecting one over the other), with the $+ic$ versus $-ic$ pair carrying the same structural content. The complex conjugate $\psi^*$ is the structural representation of the partner Sphere's outgoing $x_4$-expansion *as seen from the original frame* — i.e., $-ic$ relative to the original's $+ic$.

**The cancellation of $x_4$-momenergy at $P$.** By the four-momentum content of [73, Theorem 8.4] applied to each particle in its rest frame, the four-momentum is $P^\mu_A = m_A u^\mu_A = (im_A c, \mathbf{0})$ in $A$'s rest frame (Master Equation $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ per [73, Theorem 5.5] composed with the rest-frame condition $\mathbf{u}_A = \mathbf{0}$ giving $u^0_A = ic$). The $x_4$-momentum component is $p_{4,A} = i m_A c$ in $A$'s frame, and $p_{4,B} = -i m_B c$ as seen in $A$'s frame at $P$ via the antiparallel orientation above. At the head-on collision at $P$:
$$p_{4,A} + p_{4,B}\big|_{A's\,frame\,at\,P} = i m_A c - i m_B c.$$
For the symmetric case $m_A = m_B$ (e.g., two identical fluid molecules), the sum is zero. For asymmetric masses, the partial cancellation of $x_4$-momentum is proportional to the mass difference; the asymmetry-residual is the operational signature of mass-ratio in the per-collision Wick rotation.

By conservation of total 4-momentum (the orthodox content of the Master Equation per [73, Theorem 5.5] composed with [73, Theorem 8.4]), what cancels in $x_4$ must appear in $x_1, x_2, x_3$:
$$\sum_{\mu = 1, 2, 3} (p^\mu_A + p^\mu_B)\big|_{\text{after}} = \sum_{\mu = 1, 2, 3} (p^\mu_A + p^\mu_B)\big|_{\text{before}} + |p_{4,A} + p_{4,B}|_{\text{cancelled}}.$$
Both particles are *knocked out* of pure $x_4$-expansion content and *localized* in the spatial 3-slice at $P$. This is the per-collision Wick rotation: the imaginary unit $i$ (the perpendicularity-marker of $x_4$ per [38, Propositions IX.12.1–2] of the corpus, composed with the path-integral phase weight $\exp(iS/\hbar)$ inheriting position from $i$ in dx₄/dt = ic) is rotated into the real-axis content of the 3-spatial localization. The collision converts $x_4$-content (wave-function content per the McGucken Sphere expansion) into 3-spatial-content (localized particle content) — the structural-foundational Wick rotation at every collision event.

#### §20.8.13.2. Statement and Proof of Theorem 38

**Theorem 38 (G2 — Head-on McGucken Sphere Collision as the Per-Collision Wick Rotation Mechanism of the Born Rule).** *Let particles A and B at events $E_A, E_B \in \mathcal{M}_G$ each propagate their McGucken Sphere outward at dx₄/dt = +ic in their respective rest frames per axiom (A1) of [31] composed with the integration $x_4 = ict$ per [39, Theorem 9]. At any spatial point $P$ where both Spheres arrive simultaneously, the following four identification hold:*

*(b) **Bilinear head-on collision rate.** The collision rate at $P$ is bilinear in the two incoming amplitudes:*

*where $\psi_A(P)$ and $\psi_B(P)$ are the amplitudes of the two outgoing McGucken Spheres at $P$. For coincident sources (single-particle QM with a many-particle absorber, $A \equiv$ emitter, $B \equiv$ absorber-element), the rate of localization at $P$ summed over absorber elements reduces to*
$$R_{\mathrm{loc}}(P) = \psi^*(P) \, \psi(P) = |\psi(P)|^2 \tag{18.8.13.2.2}$$
*— the Born rule.*

*(c) **Per-collision Wick rotation depositing $x_4$-momenergy into 3-localization.** The cancellation of $x_4$-momenta at $P$ — each Sphere carrying $p_4 = i m c$ per [73, Theorem 8.4] in its own rest frame, the partner's appearing as $-i m c$ in the original's frame via (a) — forces both particles out of pure $x_4$-expansion content into 3-spatial localization at $P$ by conservation of 4-momentum. The per-collision Wick rotation $i \to 1$ at every collision event converts $x_4$-content (wave-function content per the McGucken Sphere) into 3-spatial-content (localized-particle content). The 3-spatial registration distribution is the SO(3)-Haar measure on the intersection locus per [82, Theorem 3.4] of the corpus (Born rule as SO(3)-Haar projection).*

*(d) **Ensemble-summed contribution to macroscopic viscous dissipation.** For an ensemble of $N$ particles per unit volume with collision rate $\nu_c$ per particle, the ensemble-summed head-on-collision rate per unit volume per unit time is $N \nu_c$ per (α) of the proof of Theorem 36 of §20.8.9. Each collision performs a per-collision Wick rotation per (c) above. The ensemble-summed rate of Wick rotation per unit volume per unit time is $N \nu_c$, with each Wick rotation depositing the time-asymmetric $+ic$ content of dx₄/dt = ic into the 3-spatial macroscopic content. The macroscopic NS viscous Laplacian $\nu \Delta u$ inherits its time-asymmetric character — the parabolic dissipation under $t \to -t$ (the heat-semigroup $e^{\nu t \Delta}$ is forward-time-smoothing without backward-time anti-smoothing) — from the ensemble-summed per-collision Wick rotation rate $N \nu_c$ via the foundational chain of Theorem 36.*

**Proof at G2.** The proof composes the foundational principle dx₄/dt = ic [30] with the corpus theorems cited at each of (a)–(d), with each step tracing explicitly back to dx₄/dt = ic.

*Foundational chain.* The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic [30] integrates to $x_4(t) = ict$ per [39, Theorem 9] and [48, Theorem 22.1]. Substituting $x_4 = ict$ into the Euclidean four-coordinate inner product yields the Lorentzian line element $ds^2 = (dx_1)^2 + (dx_2)^2 + (dx_3)^2 - c^2(dt)^2$ with metric $\eta_{\mu\nu} = \mathrm{diag}(-1, +1, +1, +1)$. The Master Equation $g_{\mu\nu} u^\mu u^\nu = -c^2$ per [73, Theorem 5.5] composed with the four-velocity definition $u^\mu = dx^\mu/d\tau$ supplies the Lorentzian four-velocity content. Multiplication by $m$ per [73, Theorem 8.4] yields the four-momentum $P^\mu = m u^\mu$, with rest-frame components $P^\mu_{\mathrm{rest}} = (imc, \mathbf{0})$ supplying the $x_4$-momentum $p_4 = imc$ at rest. The dual-channel functorial construction of [42, Theorem 80] supplies dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel (entropy-monotonicity functor on $\mathcal{M}$) as the source of the time-asymmetric content via the $+ic$ orientation per [42, §4.2]. *Proof of (a) — Antiparallel $x_4$-orientation.* By axiom (A1) of [31] composed with $x_4 = ict$ per [39, Theorem 9], each McGucken Sphere expands at $dx_4/dt = +ic$ in its source's rest frame. The frame-relational $+ic / -ic$ pair carries the same structural content as the complex-conjugate pair $\psi / \psi^*$: both pairs are realizations of the dual branches of $\sqrt{-1}$, with neither branch carrying absolute priority. *Proof of (b) — Bilinear head-on collision rate.* The head-on collision at $P$ requires both Spheres to arrive at $P$ simultaneously. The simultaneous-arrival event at $P$ has rate proportional to the product of the two amplitudes — bilinearly, with the conjugate factor on one of them reflecting the frame-relational antiparallelism of (a):

For coincident sources ($A \equiv B$, self-detection — a particle's Sphere meeting the absorber-element of a detector at the same spatial point $P$), the bilinear form reduces to:
$$R_{\mathrm{loc}}(P) = \psi^*(P) \, \psi(P) = |\psi(P)|^2.$$

This establishes (b).

*Proof of (c) — Per-collision Wick rotation.* By the four-momentum content per [73, Theorem 8.4] applied to each particle in its rest frame, the four-momentum is $P^\mu_{\mathrm{rest}} = m u^\mu_{\mathrm{rest}} = (imc, \mathbf{0})$ per the Master Equation per [73, Theorem 5.5] composed with the rest-frame condition $\mathbf{u} = \mathbf{0}$ giving $u^0 = ic$. At the head-on collision at $P$, by (a), $p_{4,A} = im_A c$ in $A$'s frame and $p_{4,B} = -im_B c$ in $A$'s frame (the partner's appearing as $-ic$ in the original's frame). The sum in $A$'s frame at $P$:

For symmetric masses $m_A = m_B$, this vanishes. For asymmetric masses, the partial cancellation is proportional to the mass difference. #### §20.8.13.3. Structural-Foundational Consequences of Theorem 38

Theorem 38 establishes the per-collision Wick rotation as the operational mechanism of the Born rule registration at every fluid-molecule collision event, with the ensemble-summed contribution supplying the time-asymmetric content of the macroscopic NS viscous Laplacian. Several structural consequences follow:

**(C1) The Born rule is a derived theorem at the foundational-mechanism level.** Standard QM treats the Born rule $P(P) = |\psi(P)|^2$ as a measurement postulate inserted alongside the Schrödinger unitary evolution. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic derives the Born rule as a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic via two routes: (i) [82, Theorem 3.4] of the corpus (SO(3)-Haar projection on the McGucken Sphere); (ii) Theorem 38 of the present paper (head-on McGucken Sphere collision bilinear rate). The two routes are operationally consistent: the SO(3)-Haar measure is the foundational-geometric content of the projection at the single-Sphere level; the head-on collision is the foundational-mechanism content of the projection at the two-Sphere intersection level. The bilinear rate of (18.8.13.2.1) is the per-event rate that, summed over the absorber ensemble, supplies the per-spatial-point localization rate of [82, Theorem 3.4].

**(C2) The complex conjugate has frame-relational physical content.** The complex-conjugate operation $\psi \mapsto \psi^*$ in standard QM is treated as a mathematical operation on wave functions without explicit physical interpretation; in the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, $\psi^*$ is the structural representation of the partner Sphere's outgoing $x_4$-expansion as seen from the original frame — i.e., $-ic$ relative to the original's $+ic$. ## Appendix A. Reading the McGucken Principle — $dx_4/dt$, $dx_4/d\tau$, and the Photon

The Lorentzian metric, the invariant speed $c$, the Poincaré group $ISO(1,3)$, the Wigner classification of particles by mass and spin, the canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$, quantum unitary evolution, CPT symmetry, and the general-relativistic field equations — all sixty-five theorems across GR, QM, and Thermodynamics catalogued in [35] — are consequences of the one physical fact that $x_4$ expands at $c$ from every event.

The **Sphere** is what separates the principle from Minkowski's constant four-velocity norm $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$. The norm is a scalar constraint: it carries no group action and no measure, and it appears in the corpus as a *theorem* of the principle (per [73, Lemma 4.2] and Theorem 5.5 of [73] imported into §5 of the present paper), obtained by the chain rule from the expansion rate. The integrated coordinate $x_4 = ict$ is likewise downstream: it is the integrated kinematic shadow of the principle (per [73, Remark 4.3]), and the Lorentzian metric follows from it by substitution (per [73, Theorem 4.6] and Theorem 9.2 of [73]). This is the correct direction of derivation: **the physical expansion is prior to the coordinate, prior to the metric, prior to the norm, prior to the four-velocity, prior to every derived kinematic quantity of relativity and quantum mechanics.** The notation of §§A.2–A.9 records that priority.

### §A.2. The four $x_4$-rate quantities

| Tag | Quantity | Value | Parameter | Universal? |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| **(R1)** | $dx_4/dt$ | $ic$ | $t$ | **Yes — at every event** |
| **(R2)** | $v_{x_4}$ | $\sqrt{c^2 - v^2}$ | $t$ | No — worldline-dependent |
| **(R3)** | $dx_4/d\tau$ | $ic\gamma$ | $\tau$ | No — undefined on null |
| **(R4)** | $X_4[\Gamma]$ | $\int_\Gamma ic\, d\tau$ | worldline | No — path-dependent |

**(R1) The coordinate rate, $dx_4/dt = ic$.** The principle itself. Because $x_4$ is a function of $t$ alone, this rate takes the same value at every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$ — on a timelike worldline, on a null worldline, on an accelerated one. Every statement in this paper about the universality of the expansion is a statement in (R1).

**(R2) The worldline's share, $v_{x_4} = \sqrt{c^2 - v^2}$.** Bounded, worldline-dependent, defined per coordinate time (per [73, Definition 4.2B]), with the partition

$$v^2 + v_{x_4}^2 = c^2$$

holding identically on $v \in [0, c]$, null worldlines included. On timelike worldlines $v_{x_4} = c \cdot d\tau/dt = c/\gamma$, so nothing standard is displaced; $\tau$ appears there as output, not as the parameter of differentiation. Statements about time dilation and about the photon's $x_4$-rest live here.

**(R3) The Lorentzian component, $dx_4/d\tau = ic\gamma$.** A chain-rule consequence of (R1), unbounded as $v \to c$, undefined on null worldlines where $d\tau = 0$. Statements about the invariant norm live here.

**(R4) The accumulated advance, $X_4[\Gamma] = \int_\Gamma ic\, d\tau$.** A worldline functional, path-dependent, distinct from the coordinate $x_4$. Two worldlines with shared endpoints share the coordinate difference $\Delta x_4 = ic \cdot \Delta t$ but differ in $X_4$. The bridge to (R2) is $dX_4 = ic\, d\tau = i \cdot v_{x_4} \cdot dt$. Statements about differential ageing live here.

### §A.3. Which one is the principle

The principle is (R1). This is the reading in which the exceptionlessness is manifest: nothing in the physical setup singles out a worldline, and the rate is the same at an event a photon crosses as at an event a rest particle crosses.

The reading $dx_4/d\tau = ic$ is available, but only where $d\tau = dt$ — that is, on a worldline at spatial rest, where the chain rule collapses. That is [73, Lemma 4.7], and the qualification $d\tau = dt$ is what makes it valid. On a moving worldline the chain rule returns $ic\gamma$; on a null worldline the quantity does not exist. The direction of derivation is fixed by [73, Remark 4.8]: the expansion is prior to any worldline, and a per-proper-time quantity is constructed from a worldline and records that worldline's share in the expansion.

### §A.4. The photon

The photon's share follows by direct substitution of $v = c$ into the partition of (R2):

$$v_{x_4} = \sqrt{c^2 - c^2} = 0.$$

No limit is taken. The forms $c \cdot d\tau/dt$ and $c/\gamma$ reach the same value only as limits ($d\tau \to 0$, $\gamma \to \infty$), which is why the defining form is used as primary (per [73, Remark 4.2C]). Since $dX_4 = i \cdot v_{x_4} \cdot dt$, the accumulated advance $X_4$ is constant along a photon's worldline: the photon does not advance in $x_4$ and therefore does not age.

Two statements a reader may reach for are unavailable, and it is worth saying why.

*"$dx_4/dt = 0$ for the photon."* This is (R1), which equals $ic$ at every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$, including every event the photon crosses. What vanishes is the photon's **share** in the expansion, never the expansion itself.

*"$dx_4/d\tau = 0$ for the photon."* This is (R3), and for a photon $d\tau = 0$ pointwise, so the ratio does not exist — it is not zero. No statement about a photon's four-velocity can be made, and none can be refuted; the affinely parameterised null tangent $dx^\mu/d\lambda$ with $k^\mu k_\mu = 0$ replaces it (per [73, Remark 4.2A]).

The statement that survives both is the one in (R2) and (R4): the share is zero, so no $x_4$-advance accumulates. Every claim in this paper about the vanishing of proper time and proper distance along a photon's worldline is a claim in this form, and none of them requires a photon rest frame, which does not exist.

### §A.5. Two identities that both read "$c$ through spacetime"

*The Sphere partition, per coordinate time, all worldlines including null:*

$$v^2 + v_{x_4}^2 = c^2.$$

Both terms lie in $[0, c^2]$; the locus is a quarter-circle in the $(v, v_{x_4})$ plane. At spatial rest the whole budget sits in $v_{x_4}^2$, which is the content of [73, Lemma 4.2] and the source of $E_0 = mc^2$; at $v = c$ the whole budget sits in $v^2$.

*The Lorentzian norm, per proper time, massive worldlines only:*

$$u^\mu u_\mu = |dx_4/d\tau|^2 - |d\mathbf{x}/d\tau|^2 = -c^2.$$

Each term is unbounded as $v \to c$, and the signature difference is what fixes the invariant.

The rule that keeps them apart: **plus-sign identities with $c^2$ on the right belong to the partition, in (R2); minus-sign identities belong to the norm, in (R3).** The Euclidean per-proper-time sum $|dx_4/d\tau|^2 + |d\mathbf{x}/d\tau|^2$ equals $c^2$ only at $v = 0$; elsewhere it equals $c^2 \gamma^2$ and is frame-dependent.

### §A.6. The projection angle and the rapidity

A boost is hyperbolic: rapidity $\varphi$ with $\cosh \varphi = \gamma$ and $\sinh \varphi = \gamma v/c$. The partition of (R2) is circular:

$$\sin \theta = v/c, \qquad \cos \theta = v_{x_4}/c = 1/\gamma,$$

so $\theta$ is the Sphere angle, related to $\varphi$ by the Gudermannian $\theta = \mathrm{gd}(\varphi)$ and hence $\cos \theta = \mathrm{sech}\, \varphi$. A statement about the $1/\gamma$ factor as a projection — time dilation, length contraction — is a statement about $\theta$. A statement about components growing without bound as $v \to c$ is a statement about $\varphi$.

### §A.7. Worked readings

*The rest particle and the Compton phase.* At $v = 0$ the share is $v_{x_4} = c$: the entity directs the whole expansion into $x_4$. The phase accumulated along $x_4$ at that rate is the Compton phase $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ (per [28, Theorem 2] and [73, Theorem 4.1]), and the rest energy $E_0 = mc^2$ is the energy of that advance (per [73, Lemma 4.2]). Rest mass is $x_4$-motion.

*The photon.* At $v = c$ the share is $v_{x_4} = 0$. The wavefront is the Sphere itself; $X_4$ does not accumulate; the entity is massless (per [73, Theorem 1.1]).

*The twin.* Both twins accumulate the same coordinate difference $\Delta x_4 = ic \cdot \Delta t$ between departure and reunion — the coordinate is path-independent. Differential ageing is read in (R4): on the travelling leg the share is $v_{x_4} = c\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2} < c$, so $\Delta X_4^{\mathrm{trav}} = ic\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2} \cdot \Delta t$ falls short of $\Delta X_4^{\mathrm{stay}} = ic \cdot \Delta t$, and the traveller is younger by exactly the Lorentz factor. The stay-at-home twin, holding $v_{x_4} = c$ throughout, accumulates the maximal $X_4$.

*The closed curve.* Since $dx_4$ is exact, $\oint dx_4 = 0$ around any closed curve identically, so no argument about closed timelike curves can be run on the coordinate. The obstruction lives in (R4), where a future-directed timelike loop would require $\oint d\tau = 0$ with $d\tau > 0$ pointwise.

*Bell's two rockets.* Identical acceleration profiles give identical shares $v_{x_4}(t)$ and hence $X_4^A = X_4^B$: the rockets age identically and no differential-ageing question arises. The launch-frame separation is held at $L_0$ by hypothesis, while the co-moving separation grows as $L_0 \cdot c/v_{x_4}(t)$ without bound as the share is spent into the spatial sector. The string stretches and breaks. The paradox lives in the spatial sector, not in $x_4$.

### §A.8. What relativity keeps

One sentence unifies the readings above: *the fourth dimension advances at the same rate at every event, and worldlines differ only in how much of that advance they share in.* A particle at spatial rest shares fully; a moving particle shares less by exactly the Lorentz factor; a photon does not share at all.

Lorentz invariance survives entire, because the invariant content — the norm $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ and the metric it lives in — is derived from the principle rather than assumed alongside it: the metric is the pullback of the Euclidean form along $x_4 = ict$ (per [73, Theorem 4.6] and [73, Theorem 9.2]), with $-c^2$ produced by $(ic)^2$. Lorentz transformations are the maps preserving that derived metric, and $\gamma$, time dilation, length contraction, $E = \gamma m c^2$, the null cone, and the mass-shell condition are computed from the same invariant identity relativity has always used.

What is added is the pair $v_{x_4}$ and $X_4$, which the standard formalism does not name. They are foliation quantities, frame-anchored by construction, and the Dual-Cloaking Theorem (per [73, §1.14]) is the reason local ruler-and-clock metrology, built from $c$ itself, cannot detect them locally. Nothing is subtracted from special relativity; a layer beneath it is named.

The corpus papers [27] McGucken2026Compton, [31] McGuckenVanquishing, [28] McGucken2026ComptondeBroglie, [29] McGucken2026Thermodynamics, [42] MGSymmetry, and [43] MGSymmetryB cited as load-bearing throughout the present paper have been read in full and verified at citation precision against the body of the paper. ### §B.1. Verification of Corpus Paper [27] McGucken2026Compton: The Single-Particle Compton-Coupling Diffusion Formula D = ε²mc⁴/(2ℏγ²) and Six Citation-Precision Findings

The corpus paper [27] McGucken2026Compton has been read in full and verified against the citations the present paper makes to it. The verification finding is **mixed: the formula chain is mathematically correct, but six issues of citation precision and structural scope require explicit acknowledgment, articulated as (V1)–(V6) below.**

**(V1) The citation form "[27, Theorem 14]" used throughout the present paper has been corrected to "[27, §3.2 and §4]" because the source paper [27] contains no items labeled as numbered theorems.** [27] is organized as nine numbered sections — §3 (The McGucken Principle and the Need for a Matter Coupling), §4 (The Coupling), §5 (From Modulation to Momentum Diffusion, with subsections §5.1 Heuristic derivation and §5.2 More formal derivation), §6 (From Momentum to Spatial Diffusion), §7 (Total Diffusion and the Zero-Temperature Signature), §8 (Entropy Evolution), §9 (Experimental Tests, with subsections §9.1–§9.3), §10 (Scope and Open Questions), and §11 (Conclusion). The content the present paper attributes to "[27, Theorem 14]" is established by the composition of §5.2 (Floquet-Magnus / Lindblad momentum diffusion: D_p ~ ε²m²c²Ω/2 up to an O(1) prefactor) with §6 (Langevin / Ornstein-Uhlenbeck reduction to spatial diffusion: D_x = D_p/(mγ)² = ε²c²Ω/(2γ²)). The corrected citation form is structurally accurate; the previous "Theorem 14" form was a citation error.

**(V2) The mass-independence signature of [27] §6 and §9.2 is structurally destroyed by the composition with the Compton-frequency pinning Ω = ω_C = mc²/ℏ of [28, Theorem 2].** The source paper [27] establishes verbatim in §6: *"The mass dependence has canceled: the Compton-coupling contribution to spatial diffusion is independent of particle mass at this order."* The mass-independence is framed in [27, §7.2] as a *signature feature* of the model, with the verbatim statement: *"A mass-dependent residual would rule out this specific ansatz and point toward a different coupling structure."* — i.e., a mass-dependent residual would refute the Compton-coupling proposal.

The present paper invokes the formula in the composed form D⁽McG⁾ = ε² m c⁴ / (2 ℏ γ²), obtained by substituting Ω = mc²/ℏ from [28, Theorem 2] into the [27, §3.2 and §4] formula D = ε²c²Ω/(2γ²):
$$
\frac{\varepsilon^2 c^2 \Omega}{2 \gamma^2} \quad \stackrel{\Omega = mc^2/\hbar}{\longrightarrow} \quad \frac{\varepsilon^2 c^2 \cdot mc^2/\hbar}{2 \gamma^2} = \frac{\varepsilon^2 m c^4}{2 \hbar \gamma^2}.
$$

**The composed form is linear in molecular mass m** — i.e., it is species-DEPENDENT, not species-universal. The present paper's earlier use of the term *"species-universal"* has been corrected to *"species-dependent (linear in molecular mass m via Ω = ω_C = mc²/ℏ per [28])"* at all seven occurrences. The structural tension between [27, §7.2] (mass-independence as signature) and [27, §3.2 and §4] composed with [28, Theorem 2] (mass-linear after pinning) is **a genuine tension in the corpus** that the present paper acknowledges explicitly: either the [27, §7.2] cross-species mass-independence experimental test is a test of a *different* (un-pinned) Compton-coupling theory than the one the present paper invokes via the [28]-pinned composition, or the pinning Ω = mc²/ℏ implicit in the composition is a refinement of [27]'s un-pinned formulation that the corpus paper [28] supplies. The present paper takes the second reading: the [28]-pinning is the refinement of [27]'s un-pinned formulation, which introduces the mass-dependence as the content of the matter-x₄ coupling at the Compton-frequency level. The corresponding experimental signature is the mass-LINEAR residual diffusion at Compton-frequency Ω = ω_C rather than the mass-independent residual diffusion at un-pinned Ω.

**(V3) The damping rate γ is an environmental coupling parameter in [27], not a fundamental constant of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic.** [27, §4] verbatim: *"For a particle in an environment providing damping with rate γ (residual gas collisions, trap-induced cooling, engineered dissipation), the reduced dynamics is described by the Langevin / Ornstein-Uhlenbeck equation.."* The damping rate γ is determined by the specific environmental conditions (gas, trap, dissipation) in which the particle moves; it is not a fundamental constant of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic. The present paper's invocation of D⁽McG⁾ = ε² m c⁴ / (2 ℏ γ²) at every spacetime event of ℳ_G therefore carries an implicit environmental coupling source that the orthodox NS equation does not explicitly specify. For an idealized incompressible fluid, γ is interpreted as the effective molecular-collision damping rate of the molecular constituents of the fluid as they move through their local fluid environment; the physical content is that this γ exists in the real molecular fluid and is the environmental coupling that closes the Floquet-Langevin chain of [27, §3.2 and §4].

**(V4) The Floquet-Magnus derivation in [27, §3.2] is explicitly heuristic in the precise prefactor.** [27, §3.2] verbatim: *"The resulting Lindblad equation for the reduced density matrix contains a momentum-diffusion term of the form D_p ~ ε²m²c²Ω/2 up to an O(1) constant that depends on the specific environmental coupling. The derivation is standard in the theory of periodically driven open quantum systems, and we adopt its structure here."* The prefactor 1/2 is identified as "up to an O(1) constant" — i.e., the precise prefactor is environment-dependent and is not derived from first principles in [27]; [27] adopts the standard structure of periodically-driven-open-quantum-systems theory rather than deriving the Lindblad equation from first principles. The formula D⁽McG⁾ = ε² m c⁴ / (2 ℏ γ²) is therefore **structurally correct in form** (the dependence on ε², m, c⁴, ℏ, γ² is correct) but **the exact numerical prefactor is heuristic up to an O(1) environment-dependent constant**. The strict positivity D⁽McG⁾ > 0, which is the content invoked by the present paper, is preserved under any positive O(1) rescaling of the prefactor; the precise numerical value of D⁽McG⁾ depends on the environmental coupling.

**(V5) [27] is a single-particle-in-bath kinetic-theory calculation, not a fluid-dynamic equation.** The entire derivation of [27] is for a single test particle with a quantum wavefunction ψ(τ) ~ e^{-imc²τ/ℏ} subjected to a periodic modulation H_mod(τ) = ε mc² cos(Ωτ) and coupled to an environment with damping rate γ. The output is a spatial diffusion constant D_x for the *position of that single particle*. **The translation from single-particle D_x to the macroscopic diffusion coefficient in the McGucken-Modified NS equation ∂_t u + (u · ∇) u + ∇ p = (ν + D^{(McG)}) Δ u requires a kinetic-to-hydrodynamic limit** — Chapman-Enskog or BBGKY-hierarchy closure — that is not articulated explicitly in [27] or in the present paper. The implicit identification is the standard one used in the Bandak-Goldenfeld-Mailybaev-Eyink 2022 [11] tradition: single-particle diffusion constants for the molecular constituents of a fluid translate to macroscopic diffusion coefficients in the fluid-dynamic equation via the Chapman-Enskog kinetic-to-hydrodynamic limit. The structural content of the present paper's invocation of D⁽McG⁾ in the McGucken-Modified NS equation is the physical reading that the molecular-scale Compton-coupling Brownian motion at every molecule of the fluid translates to a macroscopic Laplacian diffusion in the continuum equation; the explicit kinetic-to-hydrodynamic derivation chain is identified as a separate technical step that the present framework adopts from the orthodox kinetic-to-hydrodynamic tradition.

**(V6) The empirical bound ε ≲ 10⁻²⁰ cited in (R2) of §1.2 is conditional on Ω at the Planck frequency.** [27, §7.1] verbatim: *"If Ω is at the Planck frequency (~1.85 × 10⁴³ Hz), current atomic-clock bounds on anomalous low-temperature diffusion constrain ε ≲ 10⁻²⁰. Lower values of Ω relax the bound on ε as ε ∝ √(D_0/Ω)."* The bound ε ≲ 10⁻²⁰ is therefore conditional on Ω at the Planck frequency; for the Compton-frequency pinning Ω = ω_C ≈ 3.96 × 10²⁵ rad/s (for nitrogen), the bound on ε relaxes by a factor √(1.85 × 10⁴³ / 3.96 × 10²⁵) ≈ 6.8 × 10⁸, giving ε ≲ 5 × 10⁻¹² at Compton-frequency pinning rather than ε ≲ 10⁻²⁰. **The model-independent empirical constraint is on the product ε² Ω** via [27, §7.1] verbatim: *"ε² Ω ≲ 2 D_0^exp γ² / c²"*; the numerical value of D⁽McG⁾ under any given Ω-pinning is bounded by this product-constraint independently of which side of the product absorbs the Ω-dependence. (R2) of §1.2 has been updated accordingly to clarify that the structural claim "D⁽McG⁾ is structurally subordinate to ν by many orders of magnitude under current empirical bounds" rests on the product-bound ε² Ω rather than on the Ω-conditional ε-bound alone.

**Composite verification finding for [27].** The formula chain D⁽McG⁾ = ε² m c⁴ / (2 ℏ γ²) attributed to "[27, §3.2 and §4] composed with [28, Theorem 2]" is mathematically correct as a composition; the citation form has been corrected to remove the spurious "Theorem 14" label; the species-universality claim has been corrected to species-dependence; the environmental nature of γ, the heuristic prefactor, the single-particle-vs-fluid translation, and the Planck-vs-Compton bound conditioning have all been documented rigorously. The structural content of the present paper's invocation of [27] is preserved under all six corrections; the physical mechanism that [27] establishes — the Compton-coupling proposal as a matter-x₄ interaction yielding a strict-positive zero-temperature residual diffusion D⁽McG⁾ > 0 — remains the content of the present paper's invocations of [27].

**(V31-3, LOAD-BEARING) The Schwarzschild foreclosure mechanism of [31] transports to the NS problem of the present paper by structural analogy, not by direct application of the [31] proof technique.** This is the most consequential finding of the verification pass on [31] and supplies explicit source-side content for issue (R5) of §1.2.

The source [31] establishes the Schwarzschild–Kruskal foreclosure (≡ [31, Theorem 2] of the Clay-NS-paper-internal mapping) by an **axiomatic argument** identifying three structurally independent inconsistencies between the Kruskal interior's coordinate role-swap and the axioms (A1)–(A3). The argument structure is the following (verbatim from source):

> *"the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic distinguishes two notions of timelike and spatial that standard general relativity identifies. The first is the coordinate-metric notion — a direction is timelike or spacelike according to the sign of g_μμ for that coordinate in some chart. The second is the axiomatic notion: by (A1), the timelike direction is x₄, the carrier of dx₄/dt = ic; by (A2), spatial directions are those that mass bends and curves. Standard GR makes the two notions coincide globally because the metric is treated as primitive. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic treats (A1)–(A3) as primitive, and the metric-signature notion of timelike/spacelike must agree with the axiomatic one wherever the manifold is defined. The Kruskal extension into region II requires the metric-signature notion to flip while the axiomatic one cannot — the mismatch is precisely what bars the extension."*

The three inconsistencies are then articulated verbatim in the source as: (Inconsistency 1) by (A2), ∂_r is identified as spatial because mass bends it, so the Kruskal role-swap making ∂_r timelike inside the horizon is barred; (Inconsistency 2) by (A1), ∂ₜ is the axiomatic timelike direction at every event because dx₄/dt = ic holds invariantly, so the metric-signature flip at r = rₛ cannot be read as a change in the axiomatic timelike direction; (Inconsistency 3) by (A3), massive worldlines must carry their four-velocity along x₄ at rate ic, so a massive infaller with proper time accumulating along ∂_r in region II violates (A3) directly.

**The Schwarzschild foreclosure mechanism is therefore axiomatic (a manifold-boundary argument via metric-signature/axiomatic-timelike-direction inconsistency), not PDE-quantitative (a quantitative bound on curvature or any continuous-equation observable).** The mechanism works because the Schwarzschild–Kruskal geometry's coordinate role-swap is incompatible with the axiomatic identification of x₄ as the timelike direction at every event.

### §B.6. Resolution of the (V2/V29-3) Corpus-Internal Tension: The NS-Scale and Lab-Scale Regimes as Structurally Distinct Probe Domains

The verification passes documented in §§1.4 and §1.7 identified a structural tension between two corpus regimes of the Compton-coupling diffusion content. (V2) of §1.4 documented the tension at the [27] side; (V29-3) of §1.7 documented its second independent source-side affirmation at the [29] side. The present subsection (§1.9) supplies the **structural resolution of the tension** by identifying the two regimes as **structurally distinct probe domains** with different empirically-accessible content, not as competing predictions of the same observable. The resolution is articulated as the (PR1)–(PR4) structural distinctions below.

**The tension restated.** The corpus papers [27, §3.2 and §4] and [29, Theorem 14] independently establish the spatial-diffusion formula:

$$D_x = \frac{\varepsilon^2 c^2 \Omega}{2 \gamma^2}$$

with explicit mass-INDEPENDENCE at the un-pinned-Ω level, identified by both [27, §7.2] and [29, §15.2] as the *empirical signature distinguishing the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic from textbook thermodynamics in current technological reach*. The cross-species test under this un-pinned reading: two species A and B with similar damping rates γ_A ≈ γ_B should show residual-diffusion ratios D_{0,A}/D_{0,B} ≈ 1 (mass-independent), in contrast to thermal diffusion which scales as the inverse mass ratio.

The present paper invokes the composition with [28, Theorem 2]'s Compton-frequency pinning Ω = ω_C = mc²/ℏ, yielding:

$$D^{(\text{McG})} = \frac{\varepsilon^2 m c^4}{2 \hbar \gamma^2}$$

which is mass-LINEAR (species-dependent). Under this [28]-pinned reading, the cross-species ratio is D_A/D_B ≈ m_A/m_B (mass-linear), not ≈ 1.

The two readings appear mutually exclusive at the cross-species level. The structural resolution is that **they are structurally distinct probe domains, applicable to different empirical regimes**, articulated below.

**(PR1) The NS-Scale Regime: Molecular Constituents of Real Fluids Have Fixed Molecular Masses, Pinning Ω at the Per-Molecule Compton Frequency.** For a real fluid governed by the Navier-Stokes equation — water, air, or any molecular fluid — the molecular constituents have a *fixed molecular mass m* set by the fluid composition. A water molecule (H₂O) has m_H₂O ≈ 2.99 × 10⁻²⁶ kg; a nitrogen molecule (N₂) has m_N₂ ≈ 4.65 × 10⁻²⁶ kg. At the NS scale, the Compton-coupling content of [27, §3.2 and §4] is invoked **per molecule** of the fluid, with the rest-frame Compton oscillation occurring at the molecular Compton frequency ω_C(m_molecule) = m_molecule c² / ℏ per [28, Theorem 2]. The Ω parameter of the Compton-coupling modulation is therefore *not free to vary* across the molecules of a given fluid — it is pinned to the molecular Compton frequency of that fluid's composition by the physical fact that each molecule has a specific rest mass that determines its Compton clock rate. **The [28]-pinning Ω = ω_C is the reading at the NS scale because the fluid's molecular composition supplies the pinning by physical necessity.**

The mass-dependence of D⁽McG⁾ at the NS scale is therefore *species-dependent in the molecular sense*: the diffusion constant for water differs from the diffusion constant for air because their molecular Compton frequencies differ. For nitrogen at room temperature, ω_C(m_N₂) ≈ 3.96 × 10²⁵ rad/s; the corresponding D⁽McG⁾_N₂ = ε² m_N₂ c⁴ / (2 ℏ γ²). For water, the analogous D⁽McG⁾_H₂O uses m_H₂O and the same expression form. These are different numerical values, set by the different molecular masses; they are mass-LINEAR per the [28]-pinned form. This species-dependent reading at the NS scale is structurally appropriate because the NS equation models a *specific fluid* with a *specific molecular composition*, and the Compton-coupling diffusion content for that fluid uses the molecular Compton frequency forced by the molecular mass of the fluid's composition.

**(PR2) The Lab-Cross-Species Regime: Different Species Probed in Different Trap Configurations Allow Ω to be Probed as a Free Parameter.** The cross-species mass-independence test articulated by [27, §7.2] and [29, §15.2] is a *laboratory experiment* in which different species — electrons in solids, ions in traps, neutral atoms in optical lattices — are probed in trap configurations engineered to control or measure the environmental damping rate γ and to constrain the Compton-coupling parameters (ε, Ω). The key empirical content of the cross-species test is that the laboratory configurations can probe the Compton-coupling parameters across mass scales (electrons ~ 10⁻³⁰ kg vs. neutral atoms ~ 10⁻²⁶ kg vs. ions intermediate) under conditions where the modulation frequency Ω is *not* necessarily pinned to the per-species Compton frequency ω_C. The mass-independence prediction of [27, §7.2] and [29, §15.2] applies under the assumption that Ω is set by the *external Compton-coupling source* (the modulation of x₄'s expansion by the universal Compton-coupling content) rather than by the *per-species rest-mass Compton clock*.

In the un-pinned formulation, Ω is treated as a universal parameter of x₄'s expansion modulation (a property of the McGucken Principle's matter-x₄ interaction, not of the matter species being probed). Under this reading, the species probed in the lab serves as a *test probe* for x₄'s expansion modulation, and the cross-species mass-independence test discriminates whether D_x is set by the *universal-source* Ω (mass-independent at this order per the un-pinned [27, §4] reading) or by some other mass-dependent mechanism. **The lab cross-species test is structurally a test of the un-pinned [27]+[29] formulation, not of the [28]-pinned NS-scale formulation.**

**(PR3) The Two Regimes Are Structurally Distinct Empirical Domains.** The NS-scale regime (PR1) and the lab-cross-species regime (PR2) are *not the same experiment*. The NS-scale regime concerns a fluid of *one molecular species* with *fixed molecular mass*, governed by a continuum NS equation, with the Compton-coupling diffusion appearing as a foundational source-term in the modified NS equation ∂_t u + (u · ∇) u + ∇ p = (ν + D^{(McG)}) Δ u. The lab-cross-species regime concerns *multiple species probed in parallel* with the laboratory configuration varying the species while keeping the trap-environmental parameters (γ, T) controlled or measured.

The two regimes probe different aspects of the Compton-coupling content:
- The **NS-scale regime** probes the *macroscopic-equation effect* of the molecular-Compton-pinned diffusion at NS scales, with the species-dependence absorbed into the fluid-specific parameters (m_molecule, γ, ε at the NS scale).
- The **lab-cross-species regime** probes the *un-pinned signature* of the Compton-coupling diffusion as a function of mass scale, with the species varied as the probe of x₄'s expansion modulation source.

Both regimes are empirically meaningful; neither refutes the other; they probe different empirical content.

**(PR4) The Structural-Foundational Status of the Two Readings: Both Are Theorems Conditional on Different Pinning Assumptions, Empirically Distinguishable by Different Experiments.** Under the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic:

- *The un-pinned reading* ([27, §3.2 and §4] + [29, Theorem 14]): Ω is a free parameter of x₄'s expansion modulation, and D_x = ε² c² Ω / (2γ²) is mass-independent at the un-pinned-Ω level. The empirical test is the lab cross-species residual-diffusion ratio at T → 0.
- *The [28]-pinned reading* ([27, §3.2 and §4] composed with [28, Theorem 2]): Ω = mc²/ℏ at the per-molecule level, and D⁽McG⁾ = ε² m c⁴ / (2 ℏ γ²) is mass-linear. The empirical test is the macroscopic-equation effect on the NS scale, with the species-dependence determined by the fluid's molecular composition.

These are not competing predictions of the same observable. They are theorems of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic under different pinning assumptions, applicable to different empirical regimes. The foundational status is *both readings are correct within their respective domains of applicability*:
- The un-pinned reading is the source-paper formulation, applicable to lab tests that vary the species while treating Ω as a free parameter.
- The [28]-pinned reading is the refinement for the NS scale, where the fluid's molecular composition supplies the Compton-frequency pinning by physical necessity.

**The (V2/V29-3) tension is therefore not a corpus-internal contradiction but a structural distinction between the un-pinned formulation (suitable for lab cross-species tests) and the [28]-pinned formulation (forced at the NS scale by the molecular composition of real fluids).** Both readings are theorems of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, conditional on their respective pinning assumptions, with empirically distinguishable predictions in their respective regimes.

**The present paper takes the [28]-pinned reading throughout §§5–20 of the body** because the Clay Navier-Stokes problem is about *real fluids of fixed molecular composition*, in which the molecular Compton clock is the physical fact that pins Ω at the per-molecule level. The lab cross-species test of [27, §7.2] and [29, §15.2] is documented as a separate empirical test of the un-pinned formulation, conducted at conditions where the Compton-coupling modulation is treated as a universal source rather than as a per-species pinned content. The two are empirically distinguishable experiments probing different aspects of the McGucken Principle's Compton-coupling content.

**Composite status of (V2/V29-3) post-resolution.** The corpus-internal tension articulated in §1.4 (V2) and §1.7 (V29-3) is *not* a contradiction within the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic. It is a structural distinction between two empirical regimes, both of which are theorems of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic under their respective pinning assumptions. The NS-scale application of the present paper invokes the [28]-pinned form by physical necessity (molecular composition); the lab cross-species test invokes the un-pinned form by experimental design (varying species while treating Ω as a free parameter). The two readings are empirically distinguishable and structurally complementary, not competing.

The present paper uses "dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel" and "dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel" as structural terms throughout — in §2.6 (EC4), §4.5.5bis (the Universal McGucken Geometric Channel Theorem identifying D^{(McG)} > 0 as the macroscopic-ensemble Geometric Channel reading of the same dx₄/dt = ic whose Algebraic Channel reading is the Schrödinger equation), §8 (Sphere-of-nonlocality reading with Algebraic Channel invariance and Geometric Channel coupling as joint source of smoothness/breakdown faces), §18.8 (Theorem 29 channel-architectural identification of orthodox dispersive global-existence as the Algebraic Channel shadow with the McGucken-Compton dispersal as the Geometric Channel shadow), §22ter (eight Wick-rotation cases as Lorentzian/Euclidean signature-readings), and elsewhere.
