### §1.10.1. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Duality — The Structural Statement

**The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic Duality** is the structural fact that the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic exalts physics through **two channels** — an algebraic-symmetry reading (**dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel**) and a geometric-propagation reading (**dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel**) — with every theorem of the dx₄/dt = ic framework jointly forced by both channels acting in concert. The two channels are not two independent principles; they are two readings of one principle. The full structural-priority development of the Duality is established in the McGucken-corpus grand-unification synthesis paper [35] (where the 65 theorems of GR + QM + Thermodynamics descend from dx₄/dt = ic through the McGucken Duality), in the McGucken-corpus Bayesian-likelihood paper [34] (where the 47 theorems of GR + QM are derived along structurally-disjoint Geometric Channel and Algebraic Channel parallel chains, yielding 94 derivations and a Bayesian likelihood ratio ≳ 10¹⁴¹ in favor of the physical reality of dx₄/dt = ic), in the McGucken Symmetry / Father-Symmetry paper [42] (where every principal symmetry of physics is derived as a theorem from dx₄/dt = ic through the dual-channel architecture), and in the dedicated McGucken Duality paper [44] (where the Duality is established as a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic with the position-of-i asymmetry of Geometric Channel versus Algebraic Channel, the twelve canonical i-insertions catalogue, the three-mechanism classification, and the structural-overdetermination diagnostic). The structural content imported below is verbatim from [34, §I.5–I.6].

### §1.10.2. dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel — The Algebraic-Symmetry Reading (Verbatim Import from [34, §I.5.1, Definition 7 and Theorem 8])

**Definition 7 ([34], Algebraic Channel; verbatim).** *Algebraic Channel is the reading of (McP) that asks: what transformations leave the principle invariant? Since x₄ advances at the same rate ic from every spacetime event, in every spatial direction, at every time, (McP) is invariant under:*

- *translations along x₄ itself: x₄ ↦ x₄ + a₄ for a₄ ∈ ℂ;*
- *translations along x₁, x₂, x₃: x_j ↦ x_j + a_j for a_j ∈ ℝ and j = 1, 2, 3;*
- *translations along t: t ↦ t + a₀ for a₀ ∈ ℝ;*
- *rotations of the spatial three-coordinates: x ↦ Rx for R ∈ SO(3) (the rate has no preferred spatial direction);*
- *Lorentz boosts: (t, x) ↦ Λ(t, x) for Λ ∈ SO⁺(1,3), automatic from the i in dx₄/dt = ic via the integrated identity x₄ = ict producing the Lorentzian signature on the constraint surface.*

**Theorem 8 ([34], Poincaré invariance of (McP); verbatim).** *The combined invariance group of (McP) acting on ℳ_G is the Poincaré group ISO(1,3) = ℝ⁴ ⋊ SO⁺(1,3) at the four-dimensional level.*

**Algebraic Channel — structural content (verbatim from [34, §I.5.1 closing paragraph]).** *Algebraic Channel is the invariance-group content of (McP). Through Noether's theorem (Noether 1918; see [42] for the structural-priority statement that Noether's theorem is itself a theorem of (McP)), every continuous symmetry generates a conservation law: energy (t-translation), momentum (spatial translation), angular momentum (spatial rotation), four-momentum (Lorentz), canonical commutator [q̂, p̂] = iℏ (x₄-translation + Compton coupling), stress-energy conservation ∇_μ T^{μν} = 0 (diffeomorphism). Algebraic Channel operates uniformly in Lorentzian signature; the structural reason established in [82] is that the imaginary unit i is interior to the unitary representations exp(−isp̂/ℏ), exp(−iĤt/ℏ) and cannot be exteriorised without dissolving the algebraic content.*

### §1.10.3. dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel — The Geometric-Propagation Reading (Verbatim Import from [34, §I.5.2, Definition 9])

**Definition 9 ([34], Geometric Channel; verbatim).** *Geometric Channel is the reading of (McP) that asks: what does the principle generate when applied at every spacetime event? The McGucken Sphere M⁺(p)(t) is the wavefront generated by (McP) at p₀; every point of M⁺(p)(t) is itself a source of a new McGucken Sphere; iterating this construction generates Huygens' Principle and the iterated-sphere path structure of (McP) on ℳ_G. Formally, Geometric Channel is the wavefront-functor p ↦ M⁺(p)(·), together with its iterated composition M⁺(p)(·) ∘ M⁺(q)(·) for q ∈ M⁺(p)(·).*

**Geometric Channel — structural content (verbatim from [34, §I.5.2 closing paragraphs]).** *Geometric Channel is the wavefront content of (McP). Its derivative deliverables include the wave equation □ψ = 0, the Schwarzschild metric (Birkhoff-unique geometry preserving spherical x₄-expansion), the Schrödinger equation (short-time Huygens propagation on M⁺(p)(t)), the Feynman path integral (iterated McGucken-Sphere composition), the Wiener process and the strict Second Law (Compton coupling Wick-rotated to Euclidean signature; see [29, §3] for the strict-Second-Law derivation), and the Bekenstein–Hawking horizon entropy (x₄-mode counting on horizon spheres). The full structural-priority programme of Geometric Channel as the geometric source of physics is the subject of the McGucken Sphere paper.*

*Geometric Channel is bi-signature: it admits a Lorentzian reading (with oscillating phase weight exp(iS/ℏ) producing the Feynman path integral) and an Euclidean reading (with real positive measure weight exp(−S_E/ℏ) producing the Wiener process and horizon thermodynamics). The two are related by the McGucken–Wick rotation τ = x₄/c. The structural exteriorisability of the imaginary unit from the geometric-propagation reading is what permits Geometric Channel to bridge signatures while dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel remains Lorentzian-locked; this signature-bridging property is the content of the Signature-Bridging Theorem (imported from [82, Theorem 1]).*

### §1.10.4. The Joint Forcing (Verbatim Import from [34, §I.5.3])

**Joint forcing of the two channels (verbatim from [34, §I.5.3]).** *dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel and dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel are not two independent principles; they are two readings of one principle. ### §1.10.5. The Master-Equation Pair (Verbatim Import from [34, §I.6])

**The Master-Equation Pair (verbatim from [34, §I.6]).** *The two channels meet at two foundational equations:*

$$\text{dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel master equation:} \quad [\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar.$$

$$\text{dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel master equation:} \quad u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2.$$

DOI: https://doi.org/10.1002/cpa.3160350604. URL: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/cpa.3160350604. ePDF URL: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/epdf/10.1002/cpa.3160350604. Authors: Luis A. Caffarelli (Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences, New York University, at time of publication — subsequently University of Texas at Austin / ICES / Oden Institute), Robert V. Kohn (Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences, New York University), Louis Nirenberg (Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences, New York University; Abel Prize 2015 recipient, shared with John F. Nash Jr.). The canonical Caffarelli–Kohn–Nirenberg 1982 paper establishing the partial-regularity theorem for suitable weak solutions of the Navier–Stokes equations. The principal theorem, articulated technically per [CaffarelliKohnNirenberg1982, Theorem B]: **the one-dimensional parabolic Hausdorff measure of the singular set S of any suitable weak solution is zero, 𝒫¹(S) = 0**. The singular set S ⊆ ℝ³ × ℝ is the set of spacetime points (x, t) at which the suitable weak solution fails to be essentially bounded in any parabolic-cylinder neighborhood. The parabolic Hausdorff measure 𝒫¹ is the Hausdorff-type measure constructed using parabolic-cylinder covers Q_r(x, t) = B_r(x) × (t - r², t) rather than Euclidean balls, with the parabolic gauge |Q_r| ∼ r (the parabolic 1-dimensional measure of a parabolic cylinder of spatial radius r). The parabolic scaling — space scales as r, time scales as r² — is the natural Navier–Stokes scaling under which the equation is invariant: u(x, t) ↦ λ u(λ x, λ² t) is a symmetry of the equation. The foundational-geometric content of 𝒫¹(S) = 0: the singular set S cannot contain any smooth curve in the four-dimensional spacetime ℝ³ × ℝ with the parabolic scaling. The geometric unpacking is developed in full rigor in §15.5 of the present paper. Cited by [Fefferman2000ClayNS, p. 4] as *"the best partial regularity theorem known so far for the Navier–Stokes equation"* together with the structural-foundational acknowledgement that *"it appears to be very hard to go further."* The paper has received the two highest-level recognitions in mathematics for the body of work it is part of: (i) the 2014 Leroy P. Steele Prize for Seminal Contribution to Research by the American Mathematical Society (AMS), with the AMS citation verbatim: *"The paper has been a kind of textbook for a whole generation of Navier-Stokes researchers, motivating many of the later developments and simplifications. [It] was and remains a landmark in the understanding of the behavior of the solution to the Navier-Stokes equations and has been a great source of inspiration for a generation of mathematicians";* and (ii) the **2023 Abel Prize** awarded to Luis A. Caffarelli per [AbelPrize2023CaffarelliCitation] by the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters, with two attribution tiers: at **(AP-Tier-1)** the official Abel Committee citation (Norwegian Academy verbatim, highest mathematical authority) — *"In 1983, based on Scheffer's previous work, Caffarelli, with Kohn and Nirenberg, showed that **sets of singularities of suitable weak solutions cannot contain a curve, that is, they have to be very 'small'**";* and at **(AP-Tier-2)** the popular exposition by Alex Bellos commissioned by the Abel Prize organization for lay audiences in *A Glimpse of the Laureate's Work* — *"the singularities produced **cannot fill a curve in space time (meaning the three dimensions of space and the one dimension of time treated as four dimensions.)** The 1982 paper remains **the closest anyone has got to proving or disproving the smoothness of the Navier-Stokes equations, even after another four decades of intense research in this area**."* The Bellos popular-exposition four-dimensional spacetime framing is technically accurate (parabolic Hausdorff measure on ℝ³ × ℝ is a four-dimensional measure with the time direction weighted parabolically) — and articulates the same structural content as the Tier-1 Abel Committee citation in the four-dimensional spacetime register that the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic operates on, but as commissioned popular exposition rather than as the official Committee statement. The Abel Prize is the highest-authority international recognition for living mathematicians (alongside the age-restricted Fields Medal). Identified in §§3, 10.2 of the present paper as the structural-foundational PDE-level result that the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic operates compatibly with, with the singular-set characterisation underlying the candidate blowup point (x*, T) that Theorem 6 of §11 structurally forecloses. The Caffarelli-own articulation of the partial-regularity content in plain language is supplied verbatim by [CaffarelliVideoOdenInstitute2015]: the "pop" articulation that *"if the flow in someplace becomes infinity the points where it is infinite cannot curve in space and time, so you will never see it persist for an interval of time"* and *"A singularity appears and disappears, so if they exist they have a minimal effect because you never see them."* The Caffarelli "we don't see them" articulation is structurally convergent with Šverák's 2025 Clay plenary closing conjecture at 51:51–52:41 of [Sverak2025ClayPlenary] — both senior orthodox figures, independently, decades apart, converge on the same conclusion realized as a theorem under the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic by Theorem 16 of §15.3. **With the addition of the Abel Prize 2023 official citation [AbelPrize2023CaffarelliCitation] articulating the same structural content — at (AP-Tier-1) the Abel Committee verbatim "cannot contain a curve, that is, they have to be very 'small'" and at (AP-Tier-2) the Bellos popular-exposition verbatim on the explicit four-dimensional spacetime "with the three dimensions of space and the one dimension of time treated as four dimensions" — the convergence is established at the highest mathematical authority on the foundational-physics level where the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic operates, with attribution levels clearly distinguished between the official Abel Committee citation and the Abel-Prize-commissioned popular exposition.**

The Abel Prize is, alongside the Fields Medal (age-restricted to mathematicians under 40) and the Wolf Prize in Mathematics, one of the three highest international honors in mathematics for living mathematicians; the Abel Prize is the only one of the three carrying a substantial monetary award comparable to the Nobel Prize, and is the highest honor for which there is no age restriction.

**Source-attribution audit (essential for rigorous citation).** The 2023 Abel Prize materials comprise documents at two distinct authority levels:

**(AP-Tier-1) Official Abel Committee citation (Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters, highest mathematical authority).** The verbatim Abel Committee statement on the Caffarelli–Kohn–Nirenberg 1982 partial-regularity result, in the canonical 2023 Citation document of the Norwegian Academy: *"The incompressible Navier-Stokes equations model fluid flow, such as water. The regularity of solutions of these equations in three dimensions is one of the open Clay Millennium Problems. In 1983, based on Scheffer's previous work, Caffarelli, with Kohn and Nirenberg, showed that **sets of singularities of suitable weak solutions cannot contain a curve, that is, they have to be very 'small'**."* (Date note: the Abel Committee citation dates the work as "1983"; the actual publication appeared in 1982 in *Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics* per [CaffarelliKohnNirenberg1982].) The Abel Committee citation is the **official Norwegian-Academy-level verbatim statement** on the structural content of CKN 1982; it does not include explicit four-dimensional spacetime framing or the "closest anyone has got" assessment.

**(AP-Tier-2) Bellos's *A Glimpse of the Laureate's Work* (popular exposition commissioned by the Abel Prize organization).** Alex Bellos is a mathematics popular writer (author of *Alex's Adventures in Numberland*) commissioned by the Abel Prize organization to write the lay-audience exposition accompanying the 2023 prize announcement. The verbatim Bellos passage on the CKN 1982 result: *"In 1982 Caffarelli, together with Robert Kohn and Louis Nirenberg, proved that if the Navier-Stokes equations do produce singularities, they will disappear instantly because **the singularities produced cannot fill a curve in space time (meaning the three dimensions of space and the one dimension of time treated as four dimensions.)** The 1982 paper remains **the closest anyone has got to proving or disproving the smoothness of the Navier-Stokes equations, even after another four decades of intense research in this area**."* The Bellos passage is **popular exposition by a non-mathematician commissioned by the Abel Prize organization for lay audiences**; it is not Caffarelli's own writing, not the Abel Committee's official citation, and not a peer-reviewed mathematical statement. The four-dimensional spacetime framing — "meaning the three dimensions of space and the one dimension of time treated as four dimensions" — is Bellos's accurate-but-popular translation of the technical fact that the parabolic Hausdorff measure 𝒫¹ of [CaffarelliKohnNirenberg1982] is a four-dimensional measure on ℝ³ × ℝ with parabolic weighting on the time direction. The "closest anyone has got" assessment is Bellos's lay-audience characterization, not an official Abel Committee statement.

**Structural-foundational use in the present paper.** Both Tier-1 (the official Abel Committee citation) and Tier-2 (Bellos's popular exposition) are commissioned/issued by the Abel Prize organization and carry the institutional weight of the 2023 Abel Prize award. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic of the present paper composes with both foundationally: (i) the Abel Committee Tier-1 verbatim "cannot contain a curve, that is, they have to be very 'small'" articulation supplies the highest-authority Norwegian-Academy-level senior-orthodox-voice articulation of the structural content of CKN 1982; (ii) the Bellos Tier-2 popular-exposition four-dimensional spacetime framing is technically accurate (parabolic Hausdorff measure on ℝ³ × ℝ is a four-dimensional measure) and articulates the same content in the four-dimensional spacetime register that the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic operates on — but as commissioned popular exposition rather than as the official Abel Committee statement.

The Abel Committee chair Helge Holden articulates verbatim the structural-foundational character of Caffarelli's body of work in the press-release-level Norwegian-Academy-attributed statement: *"Caffarelli's theorems have radically changed our understanding of classes of nonlinear partial differential equations with wide applications. The results are technically virtuous, covering many different areas of mathematics and its applications."* The Abel Committee citation articulates verbatim the structural position of Caffarelli's body of work on regularity theory at Tier-1 authority: *"Over a period of more than 40 years, Luis Caffarelli has made ground-breaking contributions to ruling out or characterising singularities. This goes under the name of regularity theory and captures key qualitative features of the solutions beyond the original functional analytic set-up.. Caffarelli's theorems have radically changed our understanding of classes of nonlinear partial differential equations with wide applications. The results go to the core of the matter, the techniques show at the same time virtuosity and simplicity, and cover many different areas of mathematics and its applications."* Caffarelli's prior major recognitions for the same body of work include the Wolf Prize in Mathematics 2012, the Leroy P. Steele Prize for Lifetime Achievement in Mathematics, the Shaw Prize in Mathematical Sciences 2018, and the Leroy P. Steele Prize for Seminal Contribution to Research 2014 (specifically for the 1982 CKN partial-regularity paper [CaffarelliKohnNirenberg1982]). The 2023 Abel Prize is, on the international ranking of recognitions for living mathematicians, the highest-authority recognition of Caffarelli's body of work including the 1982 CKN partial-regularity result.

**Identified in §11 (Remark 6.1, updated), §15.3 (Remark 16.1, updated), §17.4 ((CC14)), §18.8.4 (Remark, updated), and the Abstract and §21 closure of the present paper at two distinct attribution tiers: (AP-Tier-1) the highest-authority Norwegian-Academy-attributed Abel Committee citation verbatim "cannot contain a curve, that is, they have to be very 'small'"; and (AP-Tier-2) the Abel-Prize-commissioned popular exposition by Alex Bellos articulating the same content with the natural four-dimensional spacetime framing accurate to the parabolic Hausdorff measure of [CaffarelliKohnNirenberg1982]. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic supplies the foundational-physics-foundational-mathematics realization of the structural content the Abel Committee at Tier-1 articulates as "cannot contain a curve" and the Bellos popular exposition at Tier-2 articulates as "cannot fill a curve in space time (treated as four dimensions)" — with the four-dimensional manifold ℳ_G on which dx₄/dt = ic operates being the foundational-geometric realization, of exactly the four-dimensional spacetime that Bellos's popular exposition articulates as the natural register for the foundational NS singularity content.**
